nahhas-meani:128-128.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ ٱلأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾.
Al-Zuhrī related from Sālim, from his father, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the second rakʿa of the dawn prayer invoking Allah against a group of the hypocrites, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ ٱلأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ﴾ to the end of the verse."
Anas ibn Mālik said: "The incisor-adjacent tooth (rabāʿiya) of the Prophet ﷺ was broken on the day of Uḥud, so he took the blood in his hand and began saying: How can a people prosper who have done this to their Prophet? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ ٱلأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾."
It has also been said: he sought permission to pray for their extermination, so this was revealed, because it was known that among them were some who would accept Islam; and the verse after it confirms that.
Whoever says that it is conjoined by "أَوْ" to His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفَاً﴾, then the meaning for him is: so that He may kill a party of them, or disgrace them by defeat, or turn to them in forgiveness, or punish them.
"أوْ" here may also be in the sense of "حتَّى" (until) and "إلاَّ أَنْ" (unless); but the first is preferable, because no part of the matter belongs to anyone among the creation. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لاَ تَبْكِ عَيْنُكَ إنَّمَا * نُحَاوِلُ مُلْكَاً أَوْ نَمُوتَ فَنُعْذَرَا
(So I said to him: let your eye not weep; we are only striving for a kingdom, or [until/unless] we die and are excused.)

nahhas-meani:130-130.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَآ أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَأْكُلُواْ ٱلرِّبَا أَضْعَافاً مُّضَاعَفَةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: They used to sell goods on deferred terms; when the term fell due, they would increase the price in return for granting a delay. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿لاَ تَأْكُلُواْ ٱلرِّبَا أَضْعَافاً مُّضَاعَفَةً﴾.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾.
That is: so that you may be in hope of success.
Sībawayh said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إذْهَبَا إلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إنَّهُ طَغَى. فَقُولاَ لَهُ قَوْلاً لَيِّنَاً لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَى﴾: Go, the two of you, upon your hope, your expectation and the extent of your knowledge; the [full] knowledge lies beyond that, and they had no more than that.
Al-falāḥ (success) in the language is: that a person attains what he hopes for.

nahhas-meani:133-133.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَارِعُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ وَٱلأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
It is related from Anas ibn Mālik that he said: It means "the first takbīr [of the prayer]".
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُها السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأرْضُ﴾.
There are two views on this:
One of them: that it is the breadth (ʿarḍ) itself.
Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb related that the Jews said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: You say, "a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth" — so where will the Fire be? ʿUmar said to them: Have you considered, when the day comes, where the night is; and when the night comes, where the day is?
They said: You have drawn upon what is in the Torah.
The other view: that al-ʿarḍ here is: amplitude (al-saʿa), and that is well known in the language.
In the ḥadīth: "The Prophet ﷺ said to those who fled on the day of Uḥud: You went off in it wide (ʿarīḍa)", meaning broad. And the linguists recited:
كَأَنَ بِلاَدَ اللهِ وَهْيَ عَرِيضَةٌ * عَلَى الخَائِفِ المَطْلُوبِ كِفَّهُ حَابِلِ
(As though the lands of Allah, broad as they are, were to the hunted, frightened man the [narrow] snare-loop of a trapper.)

nahhas-meani:134-134.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِي السَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَٱلْكَاظِمِينَ ٱلْغَيْظَ وَٱلْعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
Al-kaẓm in the language is: to hold back rage.
It is said: "the camel kaẓama its cud", when it held it back in its throat.
One who is filled with grief and sorrow is called kaẓīm and makẓūm, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إذْ نَادَى وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:135-135.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُواْ فَاحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فَٱسْتَغْفَرُواْ لِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾.
It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Whenever I heard a ḥadīth from the Messenger ﷺ, Allah benefited me by it as much as He willed to benefit me; and when a man from among his Companions narrated to me, I would ask him to swear an oath, and when he swore to me I believed him. Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me — and Abū Bakr spoke the truth —
he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "There is no man who commits a sin, then sleeps, then rises, purifies himself and does his purification well, then asks Allah's forgiveness, but that He forgives him." Then he recited the verse ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُواْ فَاحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فَٱسْتَغْفَرُواْ لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَن يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُواْ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: the meaning of ﴿وَلَمْ يُصِرُّواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُواْ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is: and they did not carry on.
Al-iṣrār (persistence) in the language is: binding oneself firmly to a thing. From it comes the word ṣurra (a tied purse); from it the cold is called ṣirr, as if it were the cold that reaches the heart; and from it one who has not performed the Hajj is called ṣarūra and ṣārūra, as though he holds back what he ought to spend.
Maʿbad ibn Ṣubayḥa said: "I prayed behind ʿUthmān, with ʿAlī at my side. He turned to us and said: I prayed without wuḍūʾ — ﴿وَلَمْ يُصِرُّواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُواْ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — then he went, performed wuḍūʾ and prayed."
It is related from Abū Bakr, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "He who asks Allah's forgiveness has not persisted, even if he returns [to the sin] seventy times in a day."
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: ﴿وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, that is: while they know that if they repent, Allah will turn to them in forgiveness.

nahhas-meani:137-137.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ سُنَنٌ فَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَٱنْظُرُواْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-sunan are: the landmarks. The meaning on this view is: when you travel you will see the traces of peoples who perished, so perhaps you will take heed!?

nahhas-meani:138-138.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا بَيَانٌ لِّلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةٌ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: This is a clarification from blindness, a guidance from misguidance, and an admonition from ignorance.

nahhas-meani:139-139.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَهِنُوا وَلاَ تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنْتُمُ الأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: Its meaning is: do not weaken.
Abū Jaʿfar said: [It is] from al-wahn (weakness).

nahhas-meani:140-140.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ فَقَدْ مَسَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ قَرْحٌ مِّثْلُهُ﴾.
It is read "قُرْحٌ" and it is read "قَرْحٌ", and with a fatḥa on both the qāf and the rāʾ.
So al-qarḥ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of qaraḥa yaqraḥu.
Al-Kisāʾī said: al-qarḥ and al-qurḥ are one and the same.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is as though al-qarḥ were the wounds, and al-qurḥ the pain.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَتِلْكَ ٱلأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
That is: at one time it is for the believers, so that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, may honour them, and at another time it is for the unbelievers, when the believers disobey; but when they do not disobey, then the party of Allah are the victorious.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنكُمْ شُهَدَآءَ وَٱللَّهُ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
That is: so that Allah may know the steadfastness of the believers when defeat befalls them, and how their steadfastness is.
He, Glorified is He, already knew this as the unseen, except that recompense does not fall upon knowledge of the unseen.
So the meaning is: so that He may know it as actually occurring, with the knowledge of the witnessed.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The Muslims who had not been present at Badr said: Would that we met the enemy, so that we might prove ourselves against them and fight them. [Then the Muslims met [them] on the day of Uḥud, and Allah took martyrs from among them, and they are those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned] when He said: ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنكُمْ شُهَدَآءَ﴾.
And "الظَّالِمُونَ" here are: the unbelievers, i.e. they did not take this love for themselves.

nahhas-meani:141-141.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِيُمَحِّصَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَيَمْحَقَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: "يُمَحِّصَ" means: He tests.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: I read before Abū al-ʿAbbās "Muḥammad ibn Yazīd", from al-Khalīl, that al-tamḥīṣ is: purifying (al-takhlīṣ). One says: maḥaṣahu, yamḥaṣuhu, maḥṣan, when he has purified it.
So the meaning on this view is: so that He may test the believers in order to reward them and purify them of their sins, and extirpate the unbelievers.

nahhas-meani:142-142.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَاهَدُواْ مِنكُمْ وَيَعْلَمَ ٱلصَّابِرِينَ﴾.
"لمَّا" is in the sense of "لَمْ", except that, according to Sībawayh, "لمَّا" is a reply to one who said "qad faʿala" (he has done), while "لَمْ" is a reply to one who said "faʿala" (he did).
The meaning of the verse is: while Allah has not yet known that as actually occurring from them, since He already knew it as the unseen.
It has also been said: the meaning is: there had been no jihad, so that Allah should know it.

nahhas-meani:143-143.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ ٱلْمَوْتَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَلْقَوْهُ فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said, from Mujāhid: "A group of the Muslims said after Badr: Would that there were fighting, so that we might prove ourselves and fight. Then when the day of Uḥud came, some of them fled, so Allah reproached them for that and said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ ٱلْمَوْتَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَلْقَوْهُ فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ﴾."
The implied construction (taqdīr) in Arabic is: and you used to wish for the cause of death; then [the word "cause"] was omitted, and the cause of death is fighting.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ﴾.
Some of the linguists said: while you were looking at Muḥammad.
Saʿīd al-Akhfash said: ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ is tawkīd (emphasis).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The real sense of this view is: you have seen it in reality, while you are seeing and certain.

nahhas-meani:1-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤمۤ * ٱللَّهُ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ ٱلْحَيُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾ [verses 1–2].
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ٱلْحَيُّ﴾ is the One who does not die, and ﴿ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾ is the One who does not pass away.
Mujāhid said: ﴿ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾ is the One who stands over everything, i.e. who stands over the management of everything — provision, life and death.
We have explained it at greater length than this, together with the meaning of ﴿الۤمۤ﴾, in Sūrat al-Baqara.
Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: ʿImrān ibn Bakkār informed me, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to us, saying: Shuʿayb ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Hārūn narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqama, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that he prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer and opened with Āl ʿImrān, reciting "الۤمۤ اللّّهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ الحيُّ القَيُّومُ"; in one rakʿa he recited a hundred verses, and in the second the remaining hundred.
We shall mention the basis of the i'rab (grammatical analysis), if Allah wills.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلاَ أَوْلاَدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيْئاً﴾.
That is because some people said: "شَغَلَتْنَا أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا".
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأُولَـٰئِكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
That is, they are like firewood in the Fire.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Like the doing of the people of Pharaoh.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And so it is in the language; it is said: دَأََب يَدْأَبُ when one strives at his doing. So the kāf may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying ﴿وَقُودُ النَّارِ﴾, i.e. they were punished with a punishment like that with which the people of Pharaoh were punished.
It may be attached to His saying (لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ).
And it may be attached to His saying (فَأَخَذَهُم اللهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ).
Ibn Kaysān said: It is possible — though remote — that it be attached to (كَذَّبُوا), in which case (كَذَّبُوا) contains the pronoun of the disbelievers, not the pronoun of the people of Pharaoh.
Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is: their striving in their disbelief is like the striving of the people of Pharaoh, and the kāf is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), i.e. their wont is like the wont of the people of Pharaoh.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿قُلْ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمِهَادُ﴾.
Ibn Kaysān said: ﴿سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾, i.e. say this to them; and [it is read] with yāʾ because they were absent at the time of the address.
It is possible that those whom he was commanded to inform were other than those who would be defeated.
It has been said: He was commanded to say to the Jews: The idolaters will be defeated.

nahhas-meani:3-4.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَنزَلَ ٱلتَّوْرَاةَ وَٱلإِنْجِيلَ مِن قَبْلُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ﴾ [verses 3–4].
That is, before the Qurʾān.
"التوراة" is from وَرَى and وَرَيْتُ (to kindle, to give out fire), so it is said: تَوْرَاةٌ, i.e. light and illumination.
The Basrans said: the origin of توراة is the pattern فَوْعَلة, like حَوْقَلَة; the maṣdar (verbal noun) of فَوْعَلْتُ is فَوْعَلَة. The original form in their view is "وَوْرَيَةٌ"; the first wāw was changed into a tāʾ, as it was changed in تَوْلَج — which is فَوْعَلٌ from وَلَجْتُ — and in their saying تالله; and the final yāʾ was changed into an alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa.
The Kufans said: (تَوْرَاةٌ) may be تَفْعَلة or تَفْعِلَة changed into تَفْعَلَة. But according to the Basrans تَوْقَوَة is not permissible for تَوْقِية, and the pattern تَفْعَلة is hardly found in the language except as an anomaly (shādhdh).
And "إنْجِيل" is from نَجَلْتُ الشيءَ, i.e. I brought the thing out; so the Injīl is that by which an effaced [trace] of the truth was brought out [Translator's note: the Arabic here, «فإنجيل خَرَجََ به دَارِسٌ من الحقِّ», appears corrupt; translated as written]; and from this the offspring of a man is called his نَجْل [Translator's note: the text reads «لواحد الرجل», apparently for «لولد الرجل», "a man's child"], as the poet said:
إلى مَعْشَرٍ لم يُورِثِ اللُّؤْمَ جَدُّهُمْ * أَصَاغَرِهُمْ وَكُلُّ فَحْلٍ لَهُ نَجْلُ
(To a people whose forefather did not bequeath baseness to their little ones — and every stallion has its offspring.)
Ibn Kaysān said: إنجيل is إفعيل from النّجْل. It is said: نَجَلَه أبوه, i.e. his father begot him; and نجلتُ الكلأَ بالمنجل (I cut the herbage with the sickle); and عينٌ نجلاءُ, a wide eye; likewise طعنةٌ نَجْلاَءُ, a wide thrust-wound. The plural of الإِنجيل is أناجيل, and the plural of التوراة is توارٍ.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَنزَلَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ﴾, i.e. that which separates truth from falsehood.
As one of the commentators said: "Every book of Allah is a furqān."
﴿وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾, i.e. everything is humbled before Him, by the trace of His making in it.
﴿ذُو ٱنْتِقَامٍ﴾, i.e. against whoever disbelieves in Him.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ﴾.
That is, in beauty and ugliness, completeness and deficiency; and He has wisdom in all of that.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُّحْكَمَاتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ﴾.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: the muḥkamāt (decisive verses) are the three verses ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْل مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ up to three verses, and the one in Banū Isrāʾīl: ﴿وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلاَّ تَعْبُدُوا إِلاَّ إيَّاهُ﴾.
He said: and the mutashābih (ambiguous) is what was ambiguous to them, such as "الۤمۤ" and "الۤمۤر".
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar said: the muḥkamāt are the obligations, the command and the prohibition; they are the pillar of the religion, and the pillar of everything is its "mother" (umm).
Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said something similar to this; they said: [it is] what it contains of the lawful and the unlawful, and whatever is other than that is mutashābih, one part of it confirming another.
Qatāda said something similar; he said: the muḥkam is what is acted upon.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the muḥkamāt are the abrogating verses, and the mutashābihāt are the abrogated ones.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّنَا﴾ means what was abrogated and what was not abrogated.
Ibn Kaysān said: their iḥkām (being made decisive) is their clarity and plainness; it may be their being made binding and obligatory; and it may be that they bear no meanings other than those of their words, so that no one goes astray in their interpretation.
What unites this is that everything muḥkam is perfect in its making. Iḥkām here may also be the preventing of the possibility of [multiple] interpretations; from this the ḥakama of a riding-animal (the bit-ring of the bridle) is so named, because it restrains it.
He said: "وَمَتَشَابِهَاتٌ" may mean that one expression resembles another while the meaning differs; or that two meanings resemble each other while the expression differs; or that the act of command and prohibition is ambiguous, so that this would be like the abrogating and the abrogated.
It was said: the mutashābihāt are such things as His saying the Exalted (ثَلاَثَةَ قُرُوْء).
The most comprehensive of these views is that the muḥkam is what stands by itself and needs no inference, and the mutashābih is what does not stand by itself and needs inference.
[If it is asked:] Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُّحْكَمَاتٌ﴾, yet He has said: ﴿كِتَابٌ أَحْكِمَتْ آياتُه﴾; and He said: ﴿وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ﴾, yet He has said: ﴿كِتَاباً مُتَشَابِهاً﴾? The answer is that the meaning of ﴿أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ﴾ is: all of it was made muḥkam, then it was set out in detail, so that part of it became the Mother of the Book. His saying ﴿مِنْهَ آيَاتٌ مُحْكَماتٌ﴾ does not remove wisdom from the mutashābihāt; likewise ﴿كِتَاباً مُتَشابهَاً﴾: His saying ﴿وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابَهاتٌ﴾ does not remove from the muḥkamāt their being mutashābih in the matter of wisdom; rather, the whole of it, since it is muḥkam, extends to everything detailed from it. And (وكتاباً متشابهاً) means: resembling itself in wisdom, no part of it differing from another, as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِنْد غَيْرِ اللهِ لَوَجَدوُا فِيهِ اخْتِلافَاً كَثِيراً﴾.
We have explained the meaning of ﴿مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُّحْكَمَاتٌ﴾ with the statements of the scholars on it.
This is the meaning of Ibn ʿAbbās's saying that they are what Allah has made obligatory upon His servants of His binding rulings, which no alteration or substitution has overtaken.
The muḥkam may also be whatever is a report (khabar), because abrogation does not overtake it; and the mutashābih is the abrogating and the abrogated, because they do not know the final outcome to which they will come from it. And in that there is wisdom, and one part of it resembles another in wisdom.
He the Exalted said: ﴿هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ and did not say: أُمُّهات.
Al-Akhfash said: This is a ḥikāya (reproduction of an expression).
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ because their meaning is one thing.
Ibn Kaysān said: I reckon that al-Akhfash meant this, i.e. they are the thing of which it is said: it is the Mother of the Book; i.e. each one of them is called the Mother of the Book, just as you say: أصحابك عليَّ أسَدٌ ضَارٍ ("your companions are a ravening lion against me"), i.e. each one is like a ravening lion, because they are treated as one thing in action.
From this is ﴿وَجَعَلْنا ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وأُمَّهُ آيَةً﴾, because their affair is one: she brought him forth without a male, and he has no father; so the sign was not hers except through him, nor his except through her, and He did not intend to separate him from her and say: "two signs".
Likewise ﴿هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾: He made them one thing in wisdom and clarity, and that thing is the Mother of the Book.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ﴾.
"Ayyūb related from Ibn Abī Mulayka, from ʿĀʾisha, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ﴾; he said: 'When you see those who dispute about it, they are those ones, so beware of them.'"
Ibn ʿAbbās said: They are the Khawārij.
Abū Ghālib said: Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī — having seen heads from among the heads of the Khawārij — recited ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ﴾, then said: It is these. I said: O Abū Umāma, is it something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ or something you said from your own opinion? He said: Then I would indeed be bold! — saying it three times — rather, I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not once, nor twice, nor three times.
Mujāhid said: الزيغُ is doubt, and the seeking of fitna (ibtighāʾ al-fitna) is [the seeking of] doubtful matters.
It was said: [it is] corrupting the relations between people.
We have mentioned the various uses of الفتنة.
And التأويلُ is from their saying: آل الأمْرُ إلى كذا, i.e. the matter came to such-and-such; and أوّلته تأويلاً: I made it come to it.
It was said: the difference between taʾwīl and tafsīr is that tafsīr is like the scholars' saying: الرّيبُ is doubt; and taʾwīl is like Ibn ʿAbbās's saying: the grandfather is a father — and he reflected on Allah's saying (يَا بَنِي آدَمَ).
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ وَٱلرَّاسِخُونَ فِي ٱلْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ﴾.
There is great disagreement about this verse.
Part of it: that the complete stop (al-tamām) is at His saying (إلاَّ اللَّهُ); this is the view of al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ, Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim.
Evidence for this is adduced from what Ṭāwūs related from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: "وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلهُ إلاَّ اللهُ، ويقول الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي العِلْمِ آمَنَّا بِهِ".
ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: The knowledge of those firmly grounded in knowledge ended at their saying: We believe in it.
Ibn Kaysān said: taʾwīl in the speech of the Arabs is that to which the meaning of speech leads; so its taʾwīl is what its meaning returns to, and what the matter settles upon in that ambiguous thing — will it come to pass or not? So in my view the speech is cut off [at that point] on this basis.
The meaning is: those firmly established in knowledge, who have reached what can be comprehended of it — of what Allah has permitted His creation to attain — say "We believe in it" by way of submission and assent to it, even if they have not reached knowledge of what its matter will lead to.
What indicates this is ﴿كُلٌ مِن عِنْد ربّنا﴾, i.e. the muḥkam and the mutashābih; for if all of it were the same to them, all of it would be muḥkam, and nothing of it would be attributed to the mutashābih.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, but it is on the view of whoever said: the muḥkam is what is not abrogated, such as "reports" and the summoning of the servants to tawḥīd, and the mutashābih is what admits abrogation among the obligations — the servants would not have knowledge of its taʾwīl and of what it will remain fixed upon.
And whoever takes "تَأْوِيلَهُ" in the sense of tafsīr (explanation) — because it is that to which the meaning of the speech leads — then in his view those firmly grounded in knowledge know its taʾwīl.
As Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid: Those firmly grounded in knowledge know its taʾwīl, saying: We believe in it.
Mujāhid said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I am among those who know its taʾwīl.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view, though good, this one is clearer than it, because the conjunctive wāw is most properly taken to include the second in what the first is included in, until some evidence indicates otherwise.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has praised those firmly grounded for their firmness in knowledge, which indicates that they know its taʾwīl.
And He, Majestic and Mighty is He, has said: ﴿أَفَلاَ يَتَدَبَّرُونَ القُرْآنَ﴾?
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ, he prayed for Ibn ʿAbbās and said:
"O Allah, give him understanding in the religion and teach him taʾwīl."
Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning of "ابتغائِهم تأويله" is that they sought the taʾwīl of their resurrection and their being brought back to life, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the taʾwīl of that, and its time, no one knows but Allah.
He said: The evidence for that is His saying ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُون إلاَّ تَأْوِيلَهُ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأوْيلُهُ﴾, i.e. the day they see what they were promised of resurrection, raising and punishment; ﴿يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ﴾, i.e. who abandoned it; ﴿قَدْ جَاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِالحَقِّ﴾, i.e. we have seen the taʾwīl (fulfilment) of what the messengers told us.
He said: The complete stop is ﴿وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾, i.e. no one knows when the resurrection is "except Allah".

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبَّنَا لاَ تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا﴾.
That is, do not try us with that by which we would deviate; i.e. they say this. It may also mean: Say, O Muḥammad.
It may be said: the causing of the heart to deviate is corruption and inclination away from the religion; so were they afraid — having been guided — that Allah would move them to corruption?
The answer: that they asked, since Allah had guided them, that He not try them with deeds burdensome to them so that they would be unable to do them, such as ﴿وَلَوْ أَنّا كَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنِ اقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾.
Ibn Kaysān said: They asked that they not deviate, so that Allah would cause their hearts to deviate, as in ﴿فَلَمَّا زَاغُوا أَزَاغَ اللهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾; i.e. make us firm upon Your guidance since You have guided us, and [grant] that we not deviate and so deserve that You cause our hearts to deviate.
He said: And there is another answer to it: that He, Majestic and Mighty is He, is the One who favoured them with guidance and made it known to them, so they asked Him that they continue in what they were upon, that He supply them with help from Him, and that He not leave them to themselves — He having begun [His dealings with] them with His bounty — so that their hearts would deviate. That is attributed to Him, Majestic and Mighty is He, because if He left them and did not take charge of their guidance they would go astray; so the cause of that would be His abandoning them.
He said: A comprehensive statement is that hearts belong to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He; He turns them however He wills.
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion."

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ ٱلنَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لاَّ رَيْبَ فِيهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يُخْلِفُ ٱلْمِيعَادَ﴾.
Ibn Kaysān said: ﴿لاَّ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾, i.e. its proof is established within the souls of the servants, even if they deny it, because they acknowledge the first life, before which they were nothing. So when they know of the restoration, it is binding upon them to acknowledge it and not to doubt it, because bringing into being what did not exist makes clear that the One who brings into being is able to restore.
Among the good things said about it: that the Day of Resurrection has no doubt in it, because when they witness it and see with their own eyes what they were promised in it, it will not be possible for doubt to enter them concerning it.

nahhas-meani:144-144.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلاَّ رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ﴾.
The meaning of "خَلَتْ" is: have passed away.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَفإِنْ مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ ٱنْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: If your Prophet dies or is killed, will you go back as unbelievers?
This view is good in the language; He likened it to one who goes back, walking backwards, after he had been walking forwards.
﴿وَسَيَجْزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّاكِرِينَ﴾
That is: for His having guided them and bestowed favour upon them.
It is said: "انْقَلَبَ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ" (he turned back on his heels), when he goes back from what he was upon.
The origin of this is from al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿuqbā, which are what follows a thing and must come after it; He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾. From it comes ʿaqib al-rijl (the heel of the foot); and from it one says: "I came in the ʿuqb of the month", when you came after it had passed, and "I came in its ʿaqib and its ʿaqb", when you came while some of it still remained. And from it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:145-145.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ ٱلآخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا﴾.
The meaning is: whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter through righteous deeds.
This is an understood speech whose meaning is well known, just as it is said: "So-and-so desires Paradise", when he does the deeds of its people; and that is not said of the sinner.

nahhas-meani:146-146.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن نَّبِيٍّ قَاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ﴾.
It is also read "قَاتَلَ". Whoever reads "قُتِلَ مَعَهُ", there are two views on it according to him:
One of them is related from ʿIkrima, namely that the meaning is: "And how many a prophet was killed", the speech being complete there; then He said ﴿مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ﴾ in the sense of: and with him were many «ربيون».
This is a good view according to the doctrine of the grammarians, because they permitted "رأيتُ زيداً السماء تُمطر عليه" (I saw Zayd, the sky raining on him) in the sense of: while the sky was raining on him.
The other view is that the meaning is: some of the «ربيون» were killed with him. It is well known in the language to say: "The Banū So-and-so came to me", when only some of them came to you. So the meaning on this view is: some of the «ربيون» were killed with him.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَمَا وَهَنُواْ لِمَآ أَصَابَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ضَعُفُواْ وَمَا ٱسْتَكَانُواْ﴾.
That is: those of them who remained did not weaken, just as it was read ﴿وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ عِنْدَ المَسْجِدِ الحَرَامِ حَتَّى يَقْتُلُوكُمْ فِيهِ، فَإنْ قَتَلُوكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوهُمْ﴾ in the sense of: if they kill some of you.
The first view, on which the complete stop (tamām) is at His saying "قُتِلَ", is better, and the ḥadīth points to it.
Al-Zuhrī said: Satan cried out on the day of Uḥud, "Muḥammad has been killed!", so a group of the Muslims fled.
Kaʿb ibn Mālik said: "I was the first to recognise the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I saw his eyes from beneath the helmet, so I called out at the top of my voice: This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ! He signalled to me to be silent. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن نَّبِيٍّ قَاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ﴾."
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: «الربيون» are: the many thousands.
Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «الربيون» are: the multitudes.
Ibn Zayd said: «الربيون» are: the followers.
It is well known that al-ribba is the multitude, so they are attributed (mansūb) to al-ribba. The rag in which the gaming arrows are gathered is called ribba and rubba, and al-ribāb are tribes that banded together.
Abān ibn Taghlib said: al-ribbī is: ten thousand.
Al-Ḥasan — Allah's mercy be upon him — said: They are the steadfast scholars, as though it were taken from the attribution to the Lord (al-Rabb), Blessed and Exalted is He.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَمَا وَهَنُواْ لِمَآ أَصَابَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: they did not weaken.
Al-wahn in the language is: the most severe weakness.
﴿وَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا﴾, that is: and they were not abased. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, reproached the Muslims by this, because they used to wish for fighting.
Mujāhid read, according to what is related from him: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ تَمنَّوْنَ المَوْتَ مِن قَبْلُ أَنْ تَلْقَوْهُ﴾, and it is a good reading. The meaning is: and you used to wish for death — to meet it — beforehand (min qablu), i.e. before you met it.

nahhas-meani:147-147.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ ربَّنَا ٱغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا فِيۤ أَمْرِنَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: It means the major sins.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا﴾.
That is: make us firm upon Your religion; and when He makes them firm upon His religion, they stand firm in war, as He said: ﴿فَتَزِلّ قَدَمٌ بَعْدَ ثُبُوتِها﴾.

nahhas-meani:148-148.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَآتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَحُسْنَ ثَوَابِ ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
Qatāda said: They were given victory in this world and bliss in the Hereafter.

nahhas-meani:150-150.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلِ ٱللَّهُ مَوْلاَكُمْ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلنَّاصِرِينَ﴾.
Al-mawlā is: the helper; and if He is their helper, they will not be overcome.

nahhas-meani:151-151.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَنُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلرُّعْبَ بِمَآ أَشْرَكُواْ بِٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَاناً﴾.
The Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been granted victory through terror."
Al-sulṭān is: the proof; and from it is ﴿هلَك عَنّي سُلْطَانِيهْ﴾, i.e. my proof.

nahhas-meani:152-152.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿تَحُسُّونَهُم﴾: you were killing them.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي ٱلأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ مَآ أَرَاكُمْ مَّا تُحِبُّونَ﴾.
That is: of the defeat of the enemy. And ﴿فَشلْتُمْ﴾: you lost courage.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The Prophet ﷺ ordered the archers to hold their position, and at first [the battle] went in the Prophet's ﷺ favour. Some of them said: Let us go after the spoils; and some of them said: We will hold firm. So Allah punished them by some of them being killed.
He said: We did not know that any of us desired this world until there was revealed ﴿مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلآخِرَةَ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ﴾.
He said: the meaning of ﴿لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ﴾ is: so that He might test you; and it has been said its meaning is: so that He might try you with affliction.

nahhas-meani:153-153.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلاَ تَلْوُونَ عَلَىٰ أحَدٍ﴾.
It is also read "تَصْعَدون" with a fatḥa on the tāʾ. Whoever gives it a ḍamma takes it from aṣʿada, when one sets out on a journey; and whoever gives it a fatḥa takes it from ṣaʿida (to climb) a mountain and the like.
The meaning of ﴿تَلْوُونَ﴾ is: you turn aside [to stop].
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱلرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ فِيۤ أُخْرَاكُمْ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: Its meaning is: at your rear.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَثَابَكُمْ غَمّاًً بِغَمٍّ﴾.
There are two views on this:
One of them: Mujāhid said: The first grief was the killing and the wounds, and the second grief was that a crier cried out: "Muḥammad has been killed!", so the later grief made them forget the first grief.
The other view: that they grieved the Prophet ﷺ by their disobeying him, because he had ordered them to hold firm and they went against his order; so Allah repaid them with that grief for their grieving of the Prophet ﷺ.
The meaning of ﴿فَأثَابَهم﴾ is: He brought down upon them what stood in place of a reward, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾, i.e. what stands for them in place of good tidings is a painful punishment. And Sībawayh recited:
تُرَادُ عَلَى دِمْنِ الحِيَاضِ فإنْ تَعَفْ * فَإنَّ المُنَدَّى رِحْلَةٌ فَرَكُوْبُ
(She is led to the dung-fouled water-troughs; and if she refuses, then her "watering" is a journey and then riding.)
That is: what stands in place of the watering is the journey and the riding.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لِّكَيْلاَ تَحْزَنُواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمْ وَلاَ مَآ أَصَابَكُمْ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿لِكَيْلا تَحْزَنُوا عَلَى مَا فَاتَكُمْ﴾ is that they had sought the spoils, [﴿وَلاَ مَا أَصَابَكُمْ﴾: in yourselves, of killing and wounds].

nahhas-meani:154-154.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ ٱلْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُّعَاساً﴾.
Al-amana and al-amn are one and the same, and it is a noun standing for the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar).
It is related from Abū Ṭalḥa that he said: "I looked on the day of Uḥud and saw no one but was dozing under his shield."
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿يَغْشَىٰ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْكُمْ، وَطَآئِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾.
﴿يَغْشَىٰ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْكُمْ﴾: by this party He means the believers; ﴿وَطَآئِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾: by this party He means the hypocrites.
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيْرَ ٱلْحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ﴾.
That is: they think that the cause of the Prophet ﷺ has dwindled away.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿ظَنَّ ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ﴾, that is: in their thinking they are in the position of the [people of the] Jāhiliyya.
﴿يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلأَمْرِ مِن شَيْءٍ؟ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ للَّهِ﴾.
That is: He gives victory to whom He wills and forsakes whom He wills.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُل لَّوْ كُنتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَتْلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمْ﴾.
That is: they would have gone out to an open expanse (barāz) of the land.

nahhas-meani:155-155.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْاْ مِنكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْتَقَى ٱلْجَمْعَانِ إِنَّمَا ٱسْتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ بِبَعْضِ مَا كَسَبُواْ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ﴾.
The meaning of "ٱسْتَزَلَّهُمُ" is: he sought that they should slip, as one says "istaʿjaltuhu", i.e. I sought that he should hasten. And the meaning of ﴿ٱسْتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ بِبَعْضِ مَا كَسَبُواْ﴾ is that, as has been related, Satan reminded them of their sins, so they disliked being killed before repenting; they did not dislike being killed out of obstinacy or hypocrisy, so Allah pardoned them.

nahhas-meani:156-156.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ لإِخْوَانِهِمْ إِذَا ضَرَبُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَوْ كَانُواْ غُزًّى لَّوْ كَانُواْ عِنْدَنَا مَا مَاتُواْ وَمَا قُتِلُواْ﴾.
ʿĪsā related from Ibn Abī Najīj [Translator's note: so in the text; elsewhere the name appears as Ibn Abī Najīḥ], from Mujāhid, who said: This is the saying of the hypocrite ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ ٱلْتَقَتَا فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُخْرَىٰ كَافِرَةٌ يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِّثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْيَ ٱلْعَيْنِ﴾.
The meaning is: there was for you a sign among the signs of the Prophet ﷺ, because he informed them of what had not [yet] happened.
And الفِئَةُ is a party (firqa), from their saying: فَأَوْتُ رأسه بالسيف and فَأَيْتُه, i.e. I split it.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read: ﴿تُرَوْنَهُمْ مِثلَيْهِمْ﴾ with ḍamma on the tāʾ.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related ﴿يُرَوْنَهُمْ﴾ with ḍamma on the yāʾ.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ ٱلْتَقَتَا﴾:
He said: Muḥammad ﷺ and his Companions, and the idolaters of Badr.
Abū ʿAmr rejected reading "تُرَوْنَهُمْ" with tāʾ; he said: If it were so, it would be "مِثْلَيْكُم".
Abū Jaʿfar said: That does not necessarily follow; rather it may mean: twice [the number of] your companions.
Ibn Kaysān said: the hāʾ and mīm in "تَروَنْهُمْ" refer back to ﴿وأُخْرَى كَافِرَةٌ﴾, and the hāʾ and mīm in "مِثْلَيْهِمْ" refer back to ﴿فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ﴾. This is a kind of implied pronoun reference indicated by the context of the speech, namely His saying ﴿والله يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾; so it indicates that the disbelievers were twice the Muslims as the eye saw them, while they were three times their number in count.
He said: The seeing here belongs to the Jews.
He said: Whoever says "يَرَوْنَهُمْ" with yāʾ makes the seeing belong to the Muslims: they saw the idolaters as twice themselves. The Muslims on the day of Badr were three hundred and fourteen, and the idolaters nine hundred and fifty; so the Muslims were shown the idolaters as double their number, and He had promised them that one man of them would overcome two men of the idolaters. So that was a sign: that they should see the thing otherwise than its [real] form, as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإذْ يُريكُمُوهُمْ إذِ الْتَقَيْتُم فِي أَعْيُنِكُمْ قَليَلاً، وَيُقَلِّلُكُمْ فِي أَعْيُنِهمْ، لِيَقْضِيَ الله أَمْراً كَانَ مَفْعُولاً﴾.
Ibn Isḥāq said: So as to bring them together for battle, for vengeance upon those He wished to take vengeance on, and for bestowing favour upon those of the people of His friendship on whom He wished to complete His favour.
Al-Farrāʾ said: "مِثْلَيْهِمْ" may mean three times their number.
Abū Isḥāq said: This is a matter in which the error is a "clear" error by every measure, because we understand the "like" (mithl) of a thing as equal to it, and we understand its two likes (mithlayhi) as what equals it twice.
Ibn Kaysān al-Azdī said: How can "two likes" stand in the place of "three likes"? Except that I reckon he made ﴿تَرَوْنَهُمْ﴾ refer back to the whole, then made the two likes attached to half of them, on the basis of the disbelievers being matched against the believers; i.e. they see the whole as twice them, as if the two parties were evenly matched.
He said: Those seeing here are the Jews. Al-Farrāʾ explained his view by saying: just as you say, when you have a slave: I need twice his like (mithlayhi) — then you need three.
Likewise in his view, if you say: I have a dirham, and I need twice its like, then you need three: twice its like plus the dirham, because you do not mean that the dirham should go.
But the meaning indicates the opposite of what he said, and so does the language.
For if they saw them as they [actually] were, there would be no sign in this; and the language is contrary to this, because the meaning of mithl is known through distinction.
What led al-Farrāʾ into this is that the idolaters were three times the believers on the day of Badr, so he imagined that it was not possible for them to see them except as they ordinarily were; so he interpreted it as when you say: I have a dirham and I need its like — the dirham remaining as it is — then you have come to need two dirhams. This is clear, but the meaning is not according to it. Rather, Allah showed them to them otherwise than their [actual] number, for two reasons:
One of them: that He saw benefit in that, because the believers' hearts were strengthened by it.
The other: that it was a sign for the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ ٱلشَّهَوَاتِ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَاءِ وَٱلْبَنِينَ وَٱلْقَنَاطِيرِ ٱلْمُقَنْطَرَةِ مِنَ ٱلذَّهَبِ وَٱلْفِضَّةِ﴾.
It was said: since they are pleasing, it is as though they have been adorned.
It was said: Satan adorned them.
﴿وَٱلْقَنَاطِيرِ ٱلْمُقَنْطَرَةِ﴾: القنطار in the speech of the Arabs is a large amount, taken from the tying and making firm of a thing; القنطرة (the arched bridge) is from that. And "مُقَنْطَرةٌ" means completed, as you say: آلافٌ مؤلفة (thousands upon thousands).
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَٱلْخَيْلِ ٱلْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَٱلأَنْعَامِ وَٱلْحَرْثِ﴾.
"الخَيْلِ المُسَوَّمَةِ": Mujāhid said: the beautiful.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: the grazing ones.
Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: المسوَّمة may be the marked ones.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Mujāhid's view is good, from their saying: رجلٌ وسيمٌ (a handsome man).
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's view is not excluded, from their saying: سامَتْ تَسُومُ (it grazed), and أسَمْتُها and سوَّمْتُها, i.e. I pastured them. They may be grazing, beautiful and marked, so as to be distinguished from others.
Abū Zayd said: The origin of that is that you put a tuft of wool on it, or a mark different from the rest of its body, so that it stands out from others in the pasture.
And الأنعام are camels, cattle and sheep; and الحرث is crops.
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ ٱلْمَآبِ﴾, i.e. the place of return.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ﴾.
﴿وأزواجٌ مطهَّرةٌ﴾, i.e. [purified] of impurities and menstruation.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿ٱلصَّابِرِينَ وَٱلصَّادِقِينَ وَٱلْقَانِتِينَ وَٱلْمُنْفِقِينَ وَٱلْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِٱلأَسْحَارِ﴾.
It was said: "الصَّابِرُونَ" are those who fast; and the month of Ramaḍān is called: the month of patience (shahr al-ṣabr).
The correct view is that the patient one is he who restrains himself from acts of disobedience.
And "والقانتونُّ لله" are those who pray, and "المُنْفِقُونَ" are those who give charity.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ وَٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلْعِلْمِ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: شَهِدَ means قَضَى (decreed), i.e. made known.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: The reality of this is that the witness is he who knows a thing and makes it clear; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has guided us by what He created and made clear to His Oneness.
Al-Kisāʾī read with fatḥa on "أَنَّ" in His saying ﴿أَنَّهُ لاَ إِلهَ إلاَّ هُوَ﴾ and in His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿أَنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللهِ الإِسلامُ﴾.
Abū al-ʿAbbās "Muḥammad ibn Yazīd" said: The implied construction (taqdīr) on this reading is: that the religion with Allah is Islam, because there is no god but He; then the bāʾ was omitted. Sībawayh recited:
أَمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ فَافْعَلْ مَا أُمِرْتَ بِهِ * فَقَدْ تَرَكْتُكَ ذَا مَالٍ وَذَا نَشَبِ
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded; I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
The meaning is: I commanded you to [do] good.
Al-Kisāʾī said: Put both in the accusative, meaning: Allah bore witness that He is such, and that the religion with Allah is Islam. It may also mean: Allah bore witness that there is no god but He, [and] that the religion with Allah is Islam.
Ibn Kaysān said: The second "أنَّ" is a badal (substitute) for the first, because Islam is the explanation of the meaning which is tawḥīd.
Ibn ʿAbbās read, according to what al-Kisāʾī reported: (شَهِدَ اللَّهُ إِنَّهُ لا إلَه إلاَّ هُوَ).
And he read (أَنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّه الإِسْلام). The implied construction on this reading is: Allah bore witness that the religion is Islam; then He began anew and said: Indeed, there is no god but He.
It is related from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, from his paternal uncle Abū al-Muhallab — and he was a Qurʾān reciter — that he read ﴿شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ﴾.
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿قائماً بالقسطِ﴾ means: with justice.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلإِسْلاَمُ﴾.
الإِسلامُ in the language is submission and yielding; from it comes استسلمَ الرجلُ (the man surrendered).
So the meaning of أسلَمَ is: he submitted and accepted what Muḥammad ﷺ brought.
Ibn ʿUmar related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the zakāt, pilgrimage to the House, and fasting the month of Ramaḍān."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾.
There are two views on the verse:
One of them: that the meaning is that the reckoning is near, as He the Exalted said: {وَمَا أَمْرُ السَّاعَةِ إِلاَّ كَلَمْحِ البَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ".
The other view: that His reckoning is swift, because He knows what His servants have done and does not need to think about any of it.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنْ حَآجُّوكَ فَقُلْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ للَّهِ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِ﴾.
Allah commanded him to argue against them that he follows the command of One whom they acknowledge, because they acknowledge that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is their Creator; so they were commanded to worship the One who created them alone.
The meaning of ﴿أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ﴾ is: I have surrendered myself to Allah, as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ﴾, i.e. your Lord remains.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلْ لِّلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ وَٱلأُمِّيِّينَ﴾.
Those who were given the Book are "the Jews" and "the Christians"; and the ummiyyūn are the idolaters of the Arabs — as though they were attributed to the mother (al-umm), because they are like the newborn in that they do not write.
It was said: they are attributed to Umm al-Qurā, which is Mecca.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ﴾ — it was said its meaning is: submit! Its reality is that it is by way of threat, as you say to a man: Have you escaped from me?
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُواْ فَقَدِ ٱهْتَدَواْ وَّإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلاَغُ﴾.
This was abrogated by the command to fight.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِٱلْعِبَادِ﴾, i.e. All-Seeing of what cuts off their excuse.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾.
Maʿqil ibn Abī Miskīn said: "The prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, used to come to the Children of Israel without a scripture, and they would kill them; then some of those who followed them would rise and command justice (qisṭ) — i.e. fairness — and they would be killed."
If someone says: Those who were admonished with this did not kill a prophet?
The answer to this: they were pleased with the deed of those who killed, so they were in their position; and also they fought the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions and intended to kill them, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الذِّينَ كَفَروا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلوكَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:159-159.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظّاً غَلِيظَ ٱلْقَلْبِ لاَنْفَضُّواْ مِنْ حَوْلِكَ﴾.
Al-faẓẓ in the language is: rough in manner, ill-natured. One says: faẓiẓta tafaẓẓu faẓāẓatan [Translator's note: the imperfect is vowelled "تِفظُّ" in the text]. The meaning of ﴿لاَنْفَضُّواْ مِنْ حَوْلِكَ﴾ is: they would have dispersed; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda.
It is as though it were dispersal in more than one direction. One says: "So-and-so yafuḍḍu the cover", i.e. he breaks it apart; and "I broke open (faḍaḍtu) the letter" is from this.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي ٱلأَمْرِ﴾.
Al-mushāwara (consultation) in the language is: that you bring out the opinion you have and that your companion has; and al-shuwār is the household goods that are on display. There are two views on the meaning of the verse:
One of them: that Allah ordered the Prophet ﷺ to consult them in matters about which no revelation had come, because some of them might have knowledge regarding the matter being consulted on, and people may know of the affairs of this world what the prophets do not know; but when there was revelation he did not consult them.
The other view: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ordered him to do this so as to win over their hearts by it, and so that it would be a sunna for those after him.
Aḥmad ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us: my father narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي ٱلأَمْرِ﴾. [Translator's note: the text of Ibn ʿAbbās's statement is not given after the isnad.]
Al-Ḥasan said: He ﷺ was ordered to do that so that his community would follow it as a sunna.

nahhas-meani:160-160.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن يَنصُرْكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فَلاَ غَالِبَ لَكُمْ وَإِن يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَنصُرُكُم مِّنْ بَعْدِهِ..؟﴾.
Al-khidhlān in the language is: abandonment. From it one says: "the people takhādhalū", when they separated from one another; and one says: "a khādhila gazelle", when she has gone off alone away from the herd. Zuhayr said:
بِجِيدِ مُغْزِلَةٍِ أَدْمَاءَ خَاذِلَةٍ * من الظِّبَاءِ تُراعِي شَادِنَاً خَرَقَا
(With the neck of a tawny gazelle with a fawn, one that has kept apart from the herd, watching over a young fawn startled and unsteady.)

nahhas-meani:161-161.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ﴾.
It is also read (يُغَلَّ). The meaning of ﴿يَغُلَّ﴾ is: to act unfaithfully. Abū Ṣakhr related from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, concerning the meaning of ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ﴾, that he said: He is saying: it is not for a prophet to conceal anything of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And "يُغَلُّ" admits two meanings:
One of them: that he be found to be ghāll, i.e. unfaithful, as you say "aḥmadtu the man", when you found him praiseworthy, and "aḥmaqtuhu", when you found him foolish.
They said: What strengthens this view is that it is related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said "يُغَلَّ": he hastens to the spoils lest they be taken.
The other meaning: that (يُغَلَّ) be in the sense of "يُغَلَّ منه", i.e. that he be defrauded by having something taken from him.
It is related from Qatāda that the meaning of (يُغَل) is: he is defrauded.
A third view has also been stated, which is not sound, namely that the meaning of (يُغَلَّ) is: he is accused of unfaithfulness; had it been so, it would have been yughallal.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Let me not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a bleating sheep with him, saying: O Muḥammad! and I say: I have no power to avail you anything against Allah."
Al-ghulūl in the language is: to take something from the spoils and hide it from one's companions. From it the water that runs among the trees is called ghalal, as the poet said:
لَعِبَ السُّيُولُ بِهِ فَأَصَبحَ مَاؤُهُ * غَلَلاً يُقَطَّعُ فِي أُصُولِ الخِرْوَعِ
(The torrents played with it, so that its water became a hidden trickle, cut off among the roots of the castor plants.)
From it comes al-ghilāla (a thin inner garment); and from it one says: "So-and-so taghalghala (penetrated deep) into the matter", the origin being taghallala.
From it: "In his breast there is ghill against me", i.e. rancour; and from it: "ghallaltu my beard and ghallaytuhā" (I perfumed my beard thoroughly).

nahhas-meani:162-162.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضْوَانَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَن بَآءَ بِسَخَطٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿أَفَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضْوَانَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: one who did not act unfaithfully; ﴿كَمَن بَآءَ بِسَخَطٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: like one who acted unfaithfully?
The meaning of "بَاءَ" is: he bore.

nahhas-meani:163-163.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ، وٱللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The meaning is: they have degrees with Allah. The implied construction (taqdīr) in Arabic is: they are possessors of degrees; then [the muḍāf] was omitted. The meaning is: some of them are higher in degree than others.
It has also been said: "هُمْ" refers to those who followed Allah's good pleasure and those who incurred His wrath, i.e. each one of them has the recompense of his deeds in due measure.

nahhas-meani:164-164.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَقَدْ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤمِنِينَ إِذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولاً مِّنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾.
That is: from among those whom they knew for truthfulness and trustworthiness; he brought them clear proofs, and they had never known him to lie.

nahhas-meani:165-165.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَ لَمَّا أَصَابَتْكُمْ مُّصِيبَةٌ قَدْ أَصَبْتُمْ مِّثْلَيْهَا﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Seventy men of the Muslims were killed on the day of Uḥud, and seventy of the idolaters were killed on the day of Badr and seventy were taken captive; that is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قَدْ أَصَبْتُمْ مِّثْلَيْهَا﴾ — the day of Badr and the day of Uḥud.
The meaning of ﴿قُلْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ is: by your sin and by what your hands have earned, because the archers went against the Prophet ﷺ and did not hold firm as he had ordered them.
The meaning of (أَوِ ادْفعُوا) is: swell the numbers, even if you do not fight; and the meaning of ﴿فَادْرَءُوا﴾ is: then repel. [Translator's note: these two phrases belong to verses 167 and 168.]

nahhas-meani:169-169.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمْوَاتاً بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ﴾.
It is related that the souls of "the martyrs" roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, then take shelter in lamps hung beneath the Throne.

nahhas-meani:170-170.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَرِحِينَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَلْحَقُواْ بِهِم مِّنْ خَلْفِهِمْ أَلاَّ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾.
The meaning is: they have not caught up with them in merit, even though they have merit.

nahhas-meani:171-171.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
The meaning is: and they rejoice that Allah does not let the reward of the believers be lost.
It is also read ﴿وَإنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ with a kasra on the alif, ﴿لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ المُؤْمِنيِنَ﴾, on the basis that it is cut off from what precedes.
The meaning is: and He, Glorified is He, does not let the reward of the believers be lost; then "إنّ" was brought for tawkīd (emphasis).

nahhas-meani:172-172.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَجَابُواْ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ مِن بَعْدِ مَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْقَرْحُ﴾.
ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "When the idolaters departed on the day of Uḥud and reached al-Rawḥāʾ, they urged one another to go back to fight the Muslims. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he called on his Companions to go out, and they answered the call until they reached — meaning "Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad", which is eight miles from Medina. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَجَابُواْ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ مِن بَعْدِ مَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْقَرْحُ﴾."

nahhas-meani:173-173.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُواْ لَكُمْ فَٱخْشَوْهُمْ﴾.
It has been said: by "the people" He means "Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd", whom Abū Sufyān sent to discourage the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ; and its figurative usage (majāz) in the language is that Nuʿaym and his companions are meant by it.
Ibn Isḥāq said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ ٱلنَّاسُ﴾: they were a party of ʿAbd al-Qays.
They said: Abū Sufyān and those with him are coming back against you.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَاناً﴾, that is: the intimidation increased them in faith; and they said ﴿حَسْبُنَا ٱللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ ٱلْوَكِيلُ﴾, i.e. Allah suffices us. One says: aḥsabahu, when it sufficed him.

nahhas-meani:174-174.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنْقَلَبُواْ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ لَّمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوۤءٌ﴾.
ʿIkrima said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: When they came to Badr — Abū Sufyān had said to them: Your appointment is Badr, the place where you killed our companions — the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions arrived at Badr, and the Muslims bought things there on which they made a profit.
So the meaning on this view is: ﴿فَٱنْقَلَبُواْ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ﴾ — [a favour] in their enemy's turning away, and a bounty in their trade.

nahhas-meani:175-175.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا ذٰلِكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾.
It may be asked: How does he frighten those who have taken him as patron? It is related from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī: he frightens you with his allies. It has been said: this is good in Arabic, as you say "So-and-so gives dinars", i.e. he gives people dinars. The implied construction on this view is: he frightens the believers with his allies; then the bāʾ and one of the two objects were omitted. Its parallel is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ بَأَساً شديداً﴾, the meaning being: to warn you of a severe might. And Sībawayh recited, as an example of where the bāʾ has been omitted:
أَمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ فَافْعَلْ مَا أُمِرْتَ بِهِ * فَقَدْ تَركْتُكَ ذَا مَالٍ وَذَا نَشَبِ
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded; for I have left you possessed of wealth and of property.)
His allies here are the devils. It has also been said that the meaning of ﴿يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾ is: he frightens the hypocrites with poverty so that they do not spend, because they are the most fearful.

nahhas-meani:178-178.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لأَنْفُسِهِمْ إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُوۤاْ إِثْمَاً﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: what al-Aswad related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he said: Death is better for the believer and for the unbeliever. Then he recited ﴿وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِلأبْرَارِ﴾ and ﴿إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُوۤاْ إِثْمَاً﴾.
The other view: that this verse is specific, referring to particular people who would not accept Islam, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:179-179.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّىٰ يَمِيزَ ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ﴾.
Qatāda said: until He distinguishes the unbeliever from the believer.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said, from Mujāhid: until He distinguishes the believer from the hypocrite; and this was on the day of Uḥud, in which He made clear the believer from the hypocrite, when those of the Muslims who were killed were killed.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُطْلِعَكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْغَيْبِ﴾.
That is: He does not inform you who will accept Islam and who will die in unbelief.
﴿وَلَكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَجْتَبِي مِن رُّسُلِهِ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾: Mujāhid said: that is, He makes them purely His own.

nahhas-meani:180-180.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ هُوَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ بَلْ هُوَ شَرٌّ لَّهُمْ سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُواْ بِهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
There are two views on the verse:
One of them: that the Jews are meant by it, because they were miserly in telling of the description of the Prophet ﷺ; on this view it is by way of illustration, i.e. they will have the sin hung around their necks.
The other view, which the people of ḥadīth hold: that Abū Wāʾil related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no man who has wealth and then withholds the due that is in his wealth but that on the Day of Resurrection a bald serpent will be hung around his neck." Then he recited, as confirmation of that, ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُواْ بِهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَللَّهِ مِيرَاثُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾.
The Arabs call everything that comes to a person which had been in someone else's hand: an inheritance (mīrāth). So they were addressed in terms of what they know, because Allah causes the creation to perish [Translator's note: the text reads "يُغْنِي" (enriches); "يُفْنِي" (causes to perish) appears to be intended], and He is the best of inheritors.

nahhas-meani:181-181.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّقَدْ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوْلَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ أَغْنِيَآءُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: When there was revealed ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضَاً حَسَناً فَيَضَاعِفَهُ لَهُ أَضْعَافَاً كثِيَرَةً﴾,
the Jews said: Is He poor, then, that He asks for a loan? — deceiving their weak ones by that. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿لَّقَدْ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوْلَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ أَغْنِيَآءُ﴾.
The meaning is: according to Muḥammad's statement He is poor, because He has borrowed from us. So they disbelieved by this statement, because they intended by it to give the lie to the Prophet ﷺ and to make the believers doubt Islam.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَالُواْ وَقَتْلَهُمُ ٱلأَنبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ﴾, that is: We shall record it. It is also permissible [to read] "سَيَكْتُب ما قالوا", i.e. Allah will record what they said.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ﴾, that is: the punishment of the Fire, because there is punishment that does not burn.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيباً مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
That is, an ample share; ﴿يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَىٰ كِتَابِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar "Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ" read ﴿لِيُحْكَمَ بَيْنَهُم﴾ (passive). The first reading is better, like His saying ﴿هَذَا كِتَابُنَا يَنْطِقُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالحَقِّ﴾.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُواْ لَن تَمَسَّنَا ٱلنَّارُ إِلاَّ أَيَّاماً مَّعْدُودَاتٍ﴾.
It is related that they said: We will only be punished for forty days, which are the days in which our forefathers worshipped the calf. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that this was a fabrication and a lie on their part, and He the Exalted said: ﴿وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾, i.e. what they invent of lies — as though they fashion what did not exist — from فَرَيْتُ الشِيءَ (I cut the thing out). Zuhayr said:
وَلأَنْتَ تَفْرِي مَا خَلَقْتَ * وَبَعْضُ القَوْمِ يَخْلُقُ ثُمَّ لاَ يَفْرِيِ
(Indeed you cut out what you have measured, while some people measure and then do not cut.)

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ لاَّ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾.
There is an omission (ḥadhf) in the speech.
The meaning is: So how will their state be when We gather them "for a day in which there is no doubt", i.e. no doubt that it will come to be?

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ ٱلْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي ٱلْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَنزِعُ ٱلْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَآءُ﴾.
It was said: al-mulk (dominion) here is prophethood.
It was said: it is wealth and slaves.
It was said: it is dominance.
Qatāda said: It reached me that the Prophet ﷺ asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, to give his community the dominion of Persia, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed this verse.
The meaning of ﴿تُؤْتِي ٱلْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَآءُ﴾ is: whom You will to give it; ﴿وَتَنزِعُ ٱلْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَآءُ﴾, i.e. from whom You will to take it away; then this was omitted. Sībawayh recited:
ألاَهَلْ لِهَذَا الدَّهْرِ مِنْ مُتَعَلَّلِ * عَلَى النَّاسِ، مَهْمَا شَاءَ بِالنَّاسِ يَفْعَلِ
(Is there no respite from this age for people? Whatever it wills [to do] with people, it does.)
Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is: whatever it wills to do with people, it does.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَآءُ﴾.
It is said: عزَّ when one prevails; and ذلَّ يذِلُّّ ذُلاً when one is overcome and subdued. Ṭarafa said:
بَطِيءٍ عَلَى الجُلَّى سَرِيعٍ إلى الخَنَا * ذَلِيلٍ بِأَجْمَاعِ الرِّجَالِ مُلَهَّدِ
(Slow to meet a grave matter, quick to obscenity, abased by men's fists, battered.)

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تُولِجُ ٱللَّيْلَ فِي ٱلْنَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: It is its shortening in winter and summer. So the meaning on this view is:
You decrease the night and put the decrease into the day, and You decrease the day and put the decrease into the night. [Translator's note: translated as written; the sense intended is that what is taken from one is added to the other.]
It is said: وَلَجَ، يَلِجُ ولُوجاً، وَلَجِةً when one enters. The rajaz poet said:
* "مُتَّخِذاً في ضَعَواتٍ تَوْلَجاً" *
(Taking for itself a lair among the thickets.)
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتُخْرِجُ ٱلْحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ ٱلَمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلْحَيِّ﴾.
Salmān said: That is, You bring forth the believer from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever from the believer.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said — and this is the meaning of their statement: You bring forth the sperm-drop, which is dead, from the man, who is alive; and You bring forth the man, who is alive, from the sperm-drop, which is dead.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَتَرْزُقُ مَن تَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾.
That is, without restriction or stinting, as you say: So-and-so gives without reckoning, as though he does not count what he gives.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ يَتَّخِذِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
That is, let them not take them as allies in this world, because the hypocrites displayed faith yet supported the disbelievers; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنكُم فَإنَّهُ مِنْهُم﴾.
And He said: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ أَن تَتَّقُواْ مِنْهُمْ تُقَاةً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is that one speaks with his tongue, but does not kill and does not commit a sin, his heart being at rest in faith.
Jābir ibn Zayd, Mujāhid, Ḥumayd and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read (إلاَّ أَنْ تَتَّقُوا مِنْهُمْ تَقيَّة).
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation) is with the tongue. The meaning according to most of the philologists is the same.
ʿAwf related from al-Ḥasan, who said: Taqiyya is permissible for the Muslim until the Day of Resurrection, except that he does not make taqiyya in killing.
The meaning of ﴿فَلَيْسَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ﴾ is: he is not of the party of Allah.
Sībawayh reported: هو منى فرسخين, i.e. of my companions. [Translator's note: translated as written; Sībawayh's example «هو منّي فرسخين» is usually cited as meaning "he is two parasangs away from me".]
The meaning of ﴿مِنْ دُونِ المُؤْمِنينَ﴾ is: from a place other than the place of the believers, namely the place of the disbelievers.
﴿وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ... وَالله رَوؤفٌ بِالعِبَادِ﴾.
That is, He warns you of Himself.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Love (maḥabba) in the speech of the Arabs is of various kinds: among them is love of the person [himself]. Love from Allah for His servants is forgiveness, mercy and praise of them; and love from His servants for Him is aiming at obedience to Him and being content with His laws.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿قُلْ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ فإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
The meaning is: He does not love them; then He repeated the mention [of the overt noun]. Likewise "فإنَّ اللَّهَ", and He did not say: فإنه. When the Arabs magnify a thing they repeat mention of it. Sībawayh recited:
لاَ أَرىَ المَوْتَ يَسبِقُ المَوْتَ شَيءٌ * نَغَّصَ المَوْتُ ذَا الغِنَى والفَقِيرَا
(I do not see anything outstripping death; death has embittered [life for] the rich and the poor.)

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ ءَادَمَ وَنُوحاً وَآلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَآلَ عِمْرَانَ عَلَى ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
The commentators said: The meaning is: over the world of the people of their time. The meaning of (اصْطَفَى) is: chose. This is a figurative expression, because the pure (ṣāfī) thing is that which is clear of turbidity; so the chosen ones (ṣafwa) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, are those clear of impurity, people of goodness and merit.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ عِمْرَانَ رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّراً﴾.
Khuṣayf related from Mujāhid and ʿIkrima that المحرر is the one devoted purely to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, with nothing of the affairs of this world mixed in him.
This is well known in the language: whatever is pure is called حُرٌّ (free/pure).
And مُحَرَّرٌ has its meaning. Dhū al-Rumma said:
وَالقُرْطُ فِي حُرَّةِ الذِّفْرَى مُعَلَّقَهُ * تَبَاعَدَ الحَبْلُ مِنْهُ فَهوَ يَضْطَرِبُ
(And the earring, hung on the pure-skinned spot behind the ear — its cord hangs far down, so it swings.)

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنْثَىٰ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: She only said this because only males were accepted in a vow; but Allah accepted Maryam.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلأُنْثَىٰ﴾.
There is a fronting and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the speech; the meaning is: She said, My Lord, I have delivered a female — and the male is not like the female; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ﴾.
Abū Rajāʾ, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and ʿĀṣim read ﴿وَالله أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعْتُ﴾.
On this reading, there is no fronting or postponing in the speech.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا﴾.
Qatāda said: Maryam was the daughter of ʿImrān — their imam and their chief — so they cast their arrows [as lots] over her, and the arrow of "Zakariyyā" came out; so he took charge of her (kaffalahā), i.e. took her to himself.
And in the ḥadīth: "The one who takes charge of (kāfil) the orphan shall have such-and-such."
Al-Ḥasan said: He accepted her and took on her burden.
Abū ʿUbayda said: The meaning of "كَفِلَها" is: he took her to himself, or guaranteed to undertake her care.
And His saying the Exalted: ﴿كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزْقاً﴾.
المحرابُ in the language is the high place; it is used for the noblest of places even if it is not high — except that it is related that Zakariyyā used to climb up to her by a ladder.
The meaning of ﴿وَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا رِزْقَاً﴾, on Mujāhid's view: he found with her winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
And His saying the Exalted: ﴿قَالَ يٰمَرْيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَـٰذَا﴾?
Abū ʿUbayda said: The meaning is: From where (min ayna) do you have [this]?
This statement is loose, because "أَيْنَ" is a question about places, while "أنَّى" is a question about ways and directions; the meaning is: by which of the ways and from which of the directions do you have this? Al-Kumayt distinguished between them, saying:
"أَنَّى" وَمِنْ "أَيْنَ" آبَكَ الطَّرَبُ * مِنْ حَيْثُ لاَ صَبوَةٌ وَلاَ رِيَبُ
(How, and from where, has rapture come back to you — from where there is neither youthful passion nor doubt?)
﴿قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: from Allah's side.
﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾, i.e. without stinting.

nahhas-meani:184-184.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِن كَذَّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَ رُسُلٌ مِّن قَبْلِكَ جَآءُوا بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ وَٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُنِيرِ﴾.
Al-zubur is the plural of zabūr, which is the writing (book). One says: zabartu, when I wrote.

nahhas-meani:185-185.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
This is figurative (tamthīl), and the meaning is: every soul is mortal. The linguists recited:
مَنْ لَمْ يَمُتْ عَبْطةً يَمُتْ هَرماً * لِلْمَوْتِ كأسٌ فَالْمَرْءُ ذَائِقُها
(Whoever does not die young and in health dies in old age; death has a cup, and every man is to taste it.)
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فَازَ﴾.
﴿زُحْزِحَ﴾: removed away; and ﴿فَازَ﴾: when one has been saved and is happy in the state he is in. As for their word mafāza (desert), it is only by way of good omen, just as a blind man is called baṣīr (seeing). It has also been said that mafāza is from their saying "fawwaza the man", when he died; but this view is worth nothing, because their saying "fawwaza the man" is itself also by way of good omen.

nahhas-meani:186-186.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَتُبْلَوُنَّ فِيۤ أَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾.
It has been said its meaning is: you will surely be tested; and it has been said its meaning is: you will surely be afflicted.
And the two meanings come back to one and the same thing.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوۤاْ أَذًى كَثِيراً﴾. It is related that Abū Bakr — Allah's mercy be upon him — heard a man of the Jews say: Is He poor, then, that He asks for a loan? So he slapped him, and the Jew complained of him to the Prophet ﷺ; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوۤاْ أَذًى﴾.
And «أَذًى» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) [Translator's note: the text reads "مصور", evidently for "مصدر"] of «أَذِيَ يَأْذَى», when one is hurt (taʾawwā) [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps "تأذّى" is intended].

nahhas-meani:187-187.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلاَ تَكْتُمُونَهُ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He means the Prophet ﷺ. The meaning on this view is: you shall surely make clear the matter of the Prophet ﷺ and not conceal it.
Qatāda said: "This is a covenant which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, took from the people of knowledge; so whoever knows something, let him teach it, and beware of concealing knowledge."
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَٱشْتَرَوْاْ بِهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً﴾.
﴿فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾, that is: they abandoned it. Then He made clear why they did that, saying ﴿وَٱشْتَرَوْاْ بِهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً﴾, i.e. they took bribes, and disliked following the Messenger ﷺ lest their leadership come to nothing.

nahhas-meani:188-188.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوْاْ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحْمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُواْ﴾.
It is related from Marwān that he sent to Ibn ʿAbbās, saying: Will everyone who rejoices in what he has done and loves to be praised for what he has not done be punished?
