Ibn ʿAbbās said: This is about the Jews, because the Prophet ﷺ asked them about something and they did not tell him of it, but told him of something else, [and they loved to] be praised for that, and rejoiced in what they had done in concealing [it] from the Prophet ﷺ. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوْاْ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحْمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُواْ﴾ — the verse.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr is related to have read "لاَ تَحْسِبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَا أَتَوْا", and he said: The Jews; they rejoiced in what was given to the family of Abraham of the Book, judgement and prophethood.
Then Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحْمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُواْ﴾ is their saying: We are upon the religion of Abraham.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفَازَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾.
That is: in a place of escape. ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾, that is: painful.

nahhas-meani:189-189.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَللَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾.
That is: He is their Creator and the Creator of what is in them.
This is a refutation of those who said: Allah is poor and we are rich.

nahhas-meani:190-190.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱخْتِلاَفِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ لآيَاتٍ لأُوْلِي ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾.
That is: signs pointing to Him. And al-albāb are: the intellects.

nahhas-meani:191-191.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَاماً وَقُعُوداً وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ﴾.
There are two views on the meaning of the verse:
One of them: it is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: "Whoever is unable to pray standing prays sitting, and otherwise lying on his side."
The other view: that they are those who affirm the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in every state, and remember Him. The first view does not have a sound isnad.
Moreover, Allah, Exalted is He, described the people of understanding only as remembering Him in all the states in which people are.
What makes this clear to you is the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās, when he spent the night with the Prophet ﷺ. He said: "He sat up on his bed, then raised his head to the sky, then said: 'Glory be to the King, the Most Holy' three times — and recited ﴿إنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاواتِ وَالأَرْضِ﴾ until he finished the sūra."
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is: so that this may add more to their insight.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿رَبَّنَآ مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذا بَاطِلاً﴾.
That is: they say, "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain"; so "they say" was omitted.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿سُبْحَانَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ﴾.
It is related from Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh that he said: (I asked the Prophet ﷺ about "Subḥān", and he said: [It is] declaring Allah far above evil.)
The origin of tanzīh in the language is: distance; i.e. declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, far removed from rivals and offspring.

nahhas-meani:192-192.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ ٱلنَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Azhar narrated to us by dictation, saying: Muʾammal ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, saying: Abū Hilāl narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ ٱلنَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ﴾. He said: Whoever is made to abide eternally in the Fire, You have disgraced him.
Abū al-Azhar said: And Rawḥ narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, that he recited the ḥadīth of intercession, and a man said to him: ﴿إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ ٱلنَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ﴾? He said: That is a disgrace for them.
So whoever is made to enter the Fire has been disgraced, even if he is taken out of it, because disgrace (khizy) is only the tearing away of the disgraced person's cover and his exposure. One says: khaziya yakhzā, when he is abased; and akhzaytuhu, when you abased him with an abasement that shows upon him.

nahhas-meani:193-193.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَّبَّنَآ إِنَّنَآ سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِياً يُنَادِي لِلإِيمَانِ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: It is the Qurʾān, for not all of them heard the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:194-194.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَآتِنَا مَا وَعَدتَّنَا عَلَىٰ رُسُلِكَ﴾.
Because He promised Paradise to whoever affirmed His oneness and believed.

nahhas-meani:195-195.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي لاَ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِّنْكُمْ مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَىٰ﴾.
It is also read "إِنِّي لاَ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِنْكُمْ" in the sense of: and He said: "Indeed I…"; and the fatḥa [أَنِّي] is in the sense of: that I (bi-annī) do not let the deed of any doer among you be lost, whether male or female.
It is related that Umm Salama said: O Messenger of Allah, "I have not heard Allah mention women in connection with the emigration (hijra)."
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي لاَ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِّنْكُمْ مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَىٰ بَعْضُكُم مِّن بَعْضٍ﴾.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثَوَاباً مِّن عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُ حُسْنُ ٱلثَّوَابِ﴾.
That is: a recompense. Its origin is from thāba yathūbu, when one returns; and al-tathwīb in the call to prayer is the repetition of the voice.

nahhas-meani:196-196.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ﴾.
That is: let not their free movement and their safety deceive you, for their final destination is the Fire; and one whose final destination is the Fire is not to be envied.

nahhas-meani:199-199.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَمَن يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾.
"It is related that the Prophet ﷺ prayed over al-Najāshī (the Negus) and invoked mercy upon him, and a group of the hypocrites said: He prayed over him though he is not of the people of his religion." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَمَن يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ خَاشِعِينَ للَّهِ﴾, that is: humble; and from it is the poet's saying:
* "وَإذَا افْتَقَرْتَ فَلا تَكُنْ مُتَخَشِّعَاً وَتَجَّملِ" *
("And when you become poor, do not be abject, but keep up a fine appearance.")
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لاَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً﴾.
Because He had reported that among them there were some who held fast to their religion in order to take bribes and so that their leadership would not come to nothing.

nahhas-meani:200-200.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱصْبِرُواْ، وَصَابِرُواْ، وَرَابِطُواْ﴾.
That is: be patient in your religion. ﴿وَصَابِرُوا﴾: Qatāda said: that is, outlast the idolaters in patience.
﴿ورابطوا﴾: Qatāda said: that is, wage jihad.
The origin of al-ribāṭ and al-murābaṭa according to the linguists is that the enemy tie up their horses and the Muslims tie up their horses as a precaution; then their use of it became frequent until everyone who stayed at a frontier post was called murābiṭ.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us, saying: al-Dārimī narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Jisr narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا﴾ — he said: in afflictions; ﴿وصابروا﴾ —
he said: in the five prayers; ﴿ورابطوا﴾ — the enemies of Allah in the way of Allah.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ﴾, that is: you were not commanded only to wage jihad; so fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in what He has commanded you and forbidden you.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾.
That is: so that you may be in hope of success.
The origin of al-falāḥ is: remaining and abiding forever, and we have explained it previously.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿فَنَادَتْهُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾.
It is related that Jibrīl ﷺ was the one who called him, alone.
This is not excluded in the language, as you say: So-and-so rode the ships, when he only rode one ship, i.e. he rode this kind.
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿مُصَدِّقاً بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He confirmed ʿĪsā.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He gave the glad tidings of ʿĪsā.
The meaning of "بَشَّرْتُهُ" is: I brought out joy on his skin (basharatihi).
If it is asked: What is the meaning of calling "ʿĪsā" the Word? — there are several views on this:
One of them: that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said to him "Be" and he was, He called him the Word; so the meaning on this view is: the one of Allah's Word, as He the Exalted said: ﴿واسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.
It was said: He was so named as one says: ʿAbd Allāh, and He applied it to the expression.
It was said: since the prophets had given glad tidings of him and made known that he would come without a male, and Allah gave Maryam glad tidings of him, as He said: ﴿إنَّما أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّك لأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلامَاً زَكِيَّاً﴾ — when she bore him with the description with which he had been described, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: This is My word; just as you tell a man of something, or promise it to him, and when it comes to pass you say: This is my saying (موَلي) [Translator's note: «موَلي» appears to be a misprint for «قولي», "my saying"], and this is my speech.
The Arabs call much speech, as well as a single word, a kalima; as it is related that al-Ḥuwaydira was mentioned to Ḥassān and he said: "May Allah curse that kalima of his," meaning his ode.
It was said: he was called a Word because people are guided by him as they are guided by a word.
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَسَيِّداً وَحَصُوراً وَنَبِيّاً مِّنَ ٱلصَّالِحِينَ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: السيِّدُ is the forbearing one.
It was said: the chief.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī related from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib that he recited ﴿وَسَيِّداً وَحَصُورَاً﴾, then took something [small] from the ground and said: الحصورُ is the one who does not approach women.
It is said: حُصِرَ when one is prevented; so "حَصُورٌ" means محصورٌ (prevented), as though he were prevented from what is in men.
And "فَعُولٌ" in the sense of "مَفْعُول" is frequent in the speech of the Arabs; among it is "حَلُوبٌ" in the sense of محلوبَةٌ (milked). The poet said:
فِيهَا اثْنَتَانِ وَأَرْبَعُونَ حَلُوبَةً * سُوْدَاً كخَافِيةِ الغُرَابِ الأَسْحَمِ
(Among them are forty-two milch camels, black like the hidden wing-feathers of the jet-black crow.)
It is said: حَصَرْتُ الرجلَ when I confined him; and أَحْصَرهُ المَرَضُ when illness prevented him from travelling. And الحصير (the woven mat) is named from this, because its parts are held against one another.
It was said: he is the one who restrains himself from acts of disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: [He is] the one who does not ejaculate.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلاَمٌ وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي ٱلْكِبَرُ وَٱمْرَأَتِي عَاقِرٌ﴾? [verse 40].
It may be asked: How did he find this strange, when he was a prophet who knew that Allah does what He wills?
There are two answers to this:
One of them: that the meaning is: by what rank have I merited this? — in humility before Allah.
The same was said about Maryam's saying: ﴿أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ﴾?
The other answer: that Zakariyyā wanted to know whether he would be returned to youth, and whether his wife would be returned [to youth], and whether Allah would grant them a child without being returned, or from someone other than her.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known to them that He would grant them a child without being returned, and He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ ٱللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾.
It is said: عَقُرتِ المرأة when the woman does not conceive, and عَقُرَ الرجلُ when no child is born to the man; and the male and the female are [both] عاقر.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ لِّيۤ آيَةً﴾.
That is, a sign.
﴿قَالَ آيَتُكَ أَلاَّ تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلاَّ رَمْزاً﴾.
Qatāda said: He was only punished with this because he sought a sign after the angels had addressed him directly with the glad tidings.
Mujāhid said: الرَّمْزُ is the moving of the lips.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الرَّمزُ is the moving of the hands and the head.
And الرَّمزُ in the language is a gesture, whether with the hand, the head, the eyebrow or the mouth. It is said: رَمَزَ, i.e. he gestured; and from it the immoral woman is called رامزة and رمَّازة, because she signals and does not declare openly.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ كَثِيراً وَسَبِّحْ بِٱلْعَشِيِّ وَٱلإِبْكَارِ﴾.
It was also read: "والأَبْكَارِ", which is the plural of بَكَر. It is said: بَكَر, بَكَّر, ابتكر and أبكر when one comes at the beginning of the time; and from it "الباكورة" (the first fruit) is named.
It is said: أبْكَر when one goes out between the rising of dawn and the time of forenoon.
And العشيُّ is from the time the sun declines until it sets; this is the meaning of Mujāhid's statement.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ يٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَاكِ﴾.
That is, chose you; ﴿وَطَهَّرَكِ﴾ from impurities — and it was said: from menstruation; ﴿وَٱصْطَفَاكِ عَلَىٰ نِسَآءِ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: that the meaning is: over the people of her time.
The other view: over all women, by means of ʿĪsā.
For there is no one born without a male except ʿĪsā, peace be upon him.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿يٰمَرْيَمُ ٱقْنُتِي لِرَبِّكِ﴾.
It was said: القنوتُ here is standing. It is related that the Prophet ﷺ was asked: "What is the best prayer?" and he said: "Long «قنوت»", i.e. long standing. And supplication is called «قنوت» because it is made while standing.
ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith related from Darrāj, from Abū al-Haytham, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet ﷺ — he said: he ﷺ said: "Every instance of «قنوت» that Allah mentions in the Qurʾān is obedience."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱسْجُدِي وَٱرْكَعِي مَعَ ٱلرَّاكِعِينَ﴾.
So He began with prostration before bowing. There are two answers to this:
One of them: that in their law prostration came before bowing.
The other view: that the wāw indicates combination [not sequence]; so when you say: قام زيدٌ وعمْرٌ (Zayd and ʿAmr stood), it is possible that ʿAmr was before Zayd. On this basis the meaning is: bow and prostrate. For this reason the grammarians permitted قام وزيدٌ عمروٌ [i.e. with the conjoined placed before the agent], and they recited:
أَلاَ يَا نَخْلَةً مِنْ ذَاتِ عِرْقٍ * عَلَيْكِ ـ ورحمةُ اللهِ ـ السَّلاَمُ
(O palm-tree of Dhāt ʿIrq, upon you — and the mercy of Allah — be peace.)

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿ذٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنَبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيكَ﴾.
That is, of the reports of what was hidden from you.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُون أَقْلاَمَهُمْ﴾.
﴿لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ means: with them. It was said: الأقلامُ are the arrows with which they cast lots; the arrow was called a qalam because it is pared (yuqlam), i.e. shaved.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ﴾? That is, so that they might see which of them was entitled to the guardianship of Maryam.
There is an omission in the speech, i.e. when they were disputing over her, which of them had more right to her.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَجِيهاً فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾.
الوجيهُ is the one who has standing and a lofty rank. It is said: لفلانٍ جَاهٌ وجَاهَةٌ (so-and-so has standing), and وَجُهَ يَوْجَهُ وَجَاهَةً.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَيُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِي ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلاً وَمِنَ ٱلصَّالِحِينَ﴾.
It is said: اكتهل النَّبْتُ when the plant reaches full growth. And الكَهْلُ is a man of forty, or near it.
Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb said: الكهلُ is the culmination of maturity.
The benefit in His saying the Exalted ﴿وَكَهْلاً﴾ is that He informed her that he would live until he became a man of mature age.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُ ٱلْكِتَابَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَٱلتَّوْرَاةَ وَٱلإِنْجِيلَ﴾.
It was said: it means by inspiration.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَأُبْرِىءُ ٱلأَكْمَهَ وٱلأَبْرَصَ وَأُحْيِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
﴿الأكْمَهُ﴾: Mujāhid said: he is the one who sees by day and does not see by night, so he gropes about (yatakammah).
Al-Kisāʾī said: It is said: كَمِهَ، يَكْمَهُ، كَمَهَاً.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: he is the blind.
Abū ʿUbayda said: he is the one born blind; and he recited from Ruʾba:
* "هَرَّجْتُ فَارْتَدَّ ارْتِدَادَ الأَكْمَهِ" *
(I shouted at him, and he turned back as the one born blind turns back.)
Abū ʿUbayda said concerning His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَلأُحِلَّ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾:
It may be in the sense of "all"; and he recited from Labīd:
تَرَّاكُ أَمْكِنَةٍ إِذَا لَمْ أَرْضَهَا * أَوْ يَرْتَبِطْ بَعْضَ النُّفوُسِ حِمَامُهَا
(One who readily leaves places when I am not pleased with them — or else its fated death binds some soul.)
This view is an error according to the analytical scholars among the philologists, because "some" (baʿḍ) and "part" (juzʾ) do not have the meaning of "all".
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: The meaning of "أو يَرْتَبِطْ بَعْضَ النُّفوُسِ" is: or my soul be bound, just as one says: "بَعْضُنا يعرفُه" (one of us knows him), i.e. I know him. And the meaning of the verse is on [the literal sense of] "some", because ʿĪsā ﷺ only made lawful for them some things that Mūsā had made unlawful for them, such as eating fats and others; he did not make lawful for them killing, theft or indecency.
The evidence for this is that it is related from Qatāda that he said: "ʿĪsā came to them with something gentler than what Mūsā, Allah's blessings be upon them both, came with, because Mūsā came to them with the prohibition of camels and certain fats, and ʿĪsā came to them with the permitting of some of them."

nahhas-meani:51-51.t: His saying the Exalted: ﴿فَٱعْبُدُوهُ هَـٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ﴾, i.e. this is a clear path.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿فَلَمَّآ أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْكُفْرَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿أَحَسَّ﴾ means: knew; ﴿قَالَ مَنْ أَنصَارِيۤ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Sufyān said: i.e. with Allah. Some philologists have said this, holding that the prepositions (ḥurūf al-khafḍ) may substitute for one another; and they adduced as evidence His saying the Exalted ﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنّكُم فِي جذوع النَّخْلِ﴾, saying that the meaning of "في" is the meaning of "على".
This view is not sound according to the analytical scholars, because each particle has its own meaning; two particles only coincide because of closeness of meaning. So in His saying the Exalted ﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنكُمْ فِي جُذُوع النَّخْلِ﴾:
the trunk encompassed the one crucified, and that is why "في" came in, because it had become like a container (ẓarf).
And the meaning of ﴿مَنْ أَنصَارِيۤ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾? is: Who will join his help to me to the help of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He?!
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصَارُ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās that they were only called "ḥawāriyyūn" because of the whiteness of their clothes, and they were fishermen.
Ibn Arṭāt said: They were only washers — they would whiten (yuḥawwirūn) clothes, i.e. wash them.
The philologists said: الحواريُّون are the elect of the prophets, and they are the sincere ones.
Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Al-Zubayr is my paternal aunt's son and my ḥawārī from my community," i.e. my elect. From this it is said: عين حورَاءُ when the white and the black of the eye are intense; and امرأة حوراء when her whiteness is pure along with the ḥawar of the eyes. From this the women of the Anṣār were called ḥawāriyyāt, because of their cleanliness. Abū Jilda al-Yashkurī said:
فقُلْ لِلْحَوَارِيَّاتِ يَبْكِينَ غَيْرنَا * ولا تَبْكِنَا إِلاَّ الكِلابُ النَّوَابِحُ
(So tell the fair-skinned women to weep for others than us; and let none weep for us but the barking dogs.)
And from it [comes] الحواري (fine white flour).

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿فَٱكْتُبْنَا مَعَ ٱلشَّاهِدِينَ﴾.
That is, with those who bear witness to Your Messenger by affirming [his truth].
Isrāʾīl related from Simāk ibn ʿIkrima [Translator's note: so in the text; the well-known chain is Simāk, from ʿIkrima], from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَٱكْتُبْنَا مَعَ ٱلشَّاهِدِينَ﴾.
He said: Muḥammad ﷺ and his community; they bore witness for him that he had conveyed [the message], and they bore witness for the messengers that they had conveyed [it].

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرُ ٱلْمَاكِرِينَ﴾.
This refers back to His saying the Exalted ﴿فَلَمَّا أَحَسَّ عِيسَى مِنْهُمُ الكُفْرَ﴾.
Scheming (makr) from created beings is deceit, and from Allah it is requital, as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَجَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٍ مِثْلُهَا﴾.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يٰعِيسَىٰ إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾.
There are two views on the verse:
One of them: that the meaning is: I will raise you to Me, purify you of those who disbelieve, and take you in death.
This is permissible with the wāw, because the meaning is known, and that he has not yet died.
The other view: that the meaning of "مُتَوفِّيكَ" is: taking you without death, like توفيت مالي من فلان, i.e. I took [the full amount of] my money from so-and-so; as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿اللَّـهُ يَتَوَفَّى الأَنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا، وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِها﴾.
Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: It means the taking in sleep; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, raised him in his sleep.
Maṭar al-Warrāq said: ﴿مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ﴾ are one [act], and he has not yet died.
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿متوفيك﴾, i.e. causing you to die.
Then Wahb said: Allah took him in death for three hours of the day.
And "Muḥammad ibn Jarīr" inclines to the view of those who said: I am taking you from the earth without death and raising you to Me, because of what is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "ʿĪsā son of Maryam will surely descend to the earth."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَجَاعِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
Qatāda said: It means the Muslims, because they followed him, so they will remain uppermost until the Day of Resurrection.
Others said: Those who followed him are Muḥammad ﷺ and the Muslims, because their religion is tawḥīd, just as tawḥīd was the religion of ʿĪsā ﷺ.
It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I am the closest of people to the son of Maryam."
Yūnus ibn Maysara ibn Ḥalbas related from Muʿāwiya, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "A group of my community will not cease fighting for the truth until the command of Allah comes while they are upon that." And he cited this verse as evidence: ﴿يٰعِيسَىٰ إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَجَاعِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوكَ﴾ — O Muḥammad — ﴿فَوْقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ فِيمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾.
That is, I will decide between you, and the requital will fall upon it, because it was made clear to them in this world.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَأُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَاباً شَدِيداً فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
Their punishment in this world is killing, captivity and the taking of the jizya.
And in the Hereafter, the Fire. ﴿وما لهم من ناصرين﴾, because the Muslims are above them and prevailing over them.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿ذٰلِكَ نَتْلُوهُ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ الآيَاتِ وَٱلذِّكْرِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾.
That is, of the signs which are known only by revelation or by reading a scripture. The meaning of "الحكيم" is: possessed of wisdom.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلاَ تَكُنْ مِّن ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾.
الممترون are the doubters.
If it is asked: How was the Prophet ﷺ addressed with this?
There are two answers to this:
One of them: that the meaning is: O Muḥammad, say to the doubter: This is the truth from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
The other view: that address to the Prophet ﷺ is address to all people; so the meaning on this view is: so do not [all of you] be among the doubters. What strengthens this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَاأَيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذَا طَلَّقْتُم النِّسَاءَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿فَمَنْ حَآجَّكَ فِيهِ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ فَقُلْ تَعَالَوْاْ نَدْعُ أَبْنَاءَنَا وَأَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَنِسَآءَنَا وَنِسَآءَكُمْ وَأَنْفُسَنَا وأَنْفُسَكُمْ ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ فَنَجْعَل لَّعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلْكَاذِبِينَ﴾.
It was said: by "selves" here is meant the people of their religion, as He the Exalted said: ﴿فَسَلِّموا عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾.
And He the Exalted said: ﴿فَاْقتُلوا أَنْفُسَكُم﴾. The origin of الابتهال in the language is exertion; from it is the saying of Labīd:
فِي كُهُولٍ سَادَةٍ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ * نَظَرَ الدَّهْرُ إِلَيْهِمْ فَابْتَهَلْ
(Among mature chiefs of his people — Time looked upon them and exerted itself [against them].)
That is, it exerted itself in destroying them. So the meaning of the verse is: then let us exert ourselves in supplicating for the curse.
It is related that some Christians from the people of Najrān came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he invited them to Islam. They said: We were Muslims like you. He said: You have lied; three things keep you from Islam: your saying that He has taken a son, your eating of swine's flesh, and your prostrating to the cross. They said: Who is ʿĪsā's father? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿إنَّ مَثَلَ عِيَسى عِنْدَ اللهِ كَمَثِلِ آدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِنْ تُرَابٍ﴾ up to His saying ﴿فَنَجْعَل لَّعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلْكَاذِبِينَ﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invited them to mutual cursing, and they said to one another: If you do it, the valley will blaze up against you with fire.
They said: Will you not offer us something other than this? He said: Islam, or the jizya, or war. So they accepted the jizya.
ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "Had they gone out for the mutual imprecation, they would have returned finding neither family nor children."

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْقَصَصُ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾.
That is, this which We have revealed to you is the true account; ﴿وَمَا مِنْ إِلَـٰهٍ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
"مِنْ" is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; the meaning is: there is no god but Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. The meaning of "العزيز" is the One who is not overcome, and "الحكيم" is the One possessed of wisdom.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾.
That is, All-Knowing of whoever corrupts His servants; and since He knows that, He will requite it.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿قُلْ يٰأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْاْ إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَآءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾.
The meaning of "كَلِمَةٍ" is a matter containing an explanation; then He made the word clear by His saying ﴿أَلاَّ نَعْبُدَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهَ وَلاَ نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئاً وَلاَ يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنَا بَعْضاً أَرْبَاباً مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
السَّواءُ is fairness (al-naṣafa). Zuhayr said:
أَرُونِي خُطَّة لاَ ضَيْمَ فَيهَا * يُسَوِّى بَيْنَنَا فِيهَا السَّواءُ
(Show me a course in which there is no injustice, in which fairness makes us equal.)

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿يٰأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ لِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِيۤ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَتِ ٱلتَّورَاةُ وَٱلإنْجِيلُ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾.
Because the Jews said: Ibrāhīm was one of us; and the Christians said: He was one of us. So Allah made known that Judaism and Christianity came after Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, and that the religion of Ibrāhīm is Islam, because Islam is tawḥīd, and it is the religion of all the prophets.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَكِن كَانَ حَنِيفاً مُّسْلِماً﴾.
الحَنَفُ in the language is the turning of the front of one foot towards the other, when that is congenital.
So the meaning of al-ḥanīf is the one inclining to Islam in its reality.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ أَوْلَى ٱلنَّاسِ بِإِبْرَاهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ وَهَـٰذَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
The meaning is: and the Prophet and those who believe are closest to Ibrāhīm; by "the Prophet" He means Muḥammad ﷺ.
The meaning of ﴿وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ is: their Helper.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَدَّت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَوْ يُضِلُّونَكُمْ﴾.
All of them are like this; "مِنْ" here is only for explaining the genus (bayān al-jins). It has [also] been said that "a party" means some of them.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿يٰأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ﴾.
That is, while you bear witness that they are true, because you used to give the glad tidings of the Prophet ﷺ before he was sent.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿يٰأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَلْبِسُونَ ٱلْحَقَّ بِٱلْبَاطِلِ﴾.
That is, why do you cover over [the truth]?

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَقَالَتْ طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ آمِنُواْ بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُنْزِلَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَجْهَ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱكْفُرُوۤاْ آخِرَهُ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.
الطائفةُ is a party; and وجهُ النَّهَارِ is its beginning. The poet said:
وَتُضيءُ فِي وَجْهِ النَّهَارِ مُنِيرَةً * كُجُمَانَةِ البَحْرِيَّ سُلَّ نِظَامُهَا
(She shines at the face of the day, radiant, like the pearl of the sea-diver whose string has been drawn out.)
Qatāda said: Some of the Jews said: Show Muḥammad acceptance of what he brought at the beginning of the day, then deny that at its end; for that is more likely to make it be imagined that you only did so because of something that became apparent to you which you reject, and more likely to make his companions turn back.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ تُؤْمِنُوۤاْ إِلاَّ لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ - قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْهُدَىٰ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ - أَن يُؤْتَىۤ أَحَدٌ مِّثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمْ، أَوْ يُحَآجُّوكُمْ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: There is a fronting and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the speech; the meaning is: Do not believe — except for one who follows your religion — that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, or that they will argue with you before your Lord; say: The guidance is the guidance of Allah.
It was said the meaning is: Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, except one who follows your religion; and the lām is redundant (zāʾida).
And the meaning is: Do not believe that anyone will be given, of the knowledge of the Prophet's message, the like of what you were given.
It was said the meaning is: Say, the guidance is the guidance of Allah, that anyone be given the like of what you were given; i.e. the guidance is the guidance of Allah, and it is far from the disbelievers.
Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and ʿĪsā read: ﴿أَأَنْ يُؤتَى أَحدٌ مِثْلَ مَا أُوتِيتُم﴾, and the meaning is: Is it because anyone is given the like of what you were given?
Al-Aʿmash read: ﴿إِنْ يُؤتَى أَحَدٌ مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيتُم﴾, and the meaning of "إِنْ" is the meaning of "ما" (negation), as He the Exalted said: ﴿إنِ الكافِرُونَ إلاَّ فِي غُرُورٍ﴾.
Some of the grammarians have claimed that this is a solecism (laḥn), because His saying the Exalted ﴿يُحَاجُّوكُم﴾ is without the nūn, and it ought to have been "يحاجونكم", there being nothing governing it. This view is worthless, because "أَنْ" is implied after "أو" when it has the meaning of "حتَّى" (until) and "إلاَّ أنْ" (unless), as the poet said:
فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لا تَبْكِ عَيْنُكَ إِنَّمَا * نُحَاولُ مُلْكَاً أَوْ نَمُوتَ فَنُعْذَرَا
(I said to him: Let your eye not weep; we are only striving for a kingdom — or else we die and are excused.)
It was said: the meaning of ﴿أَن يُؤْتَىۤ أَحَدٌ مِّثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمْ﴾ is: do not believe that prophethood can be [found] except among you. The proponent of this view adduced as evidence that Mujāhid said, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, after this, ﴿يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾, that it means prophethood.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِن تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
There is disagreement about the meaning of القنطار. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan that they both said: the qinṭār is a thousand mithqāls.
Abū Ṣāliḥ and Qatāda said: the qinṭār is a hundred raṭls.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ and Layth related from Mujāhid, who said: the qinṭār is seventy thousand dinars.
Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAmr related from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ al-Makkī, who said: the qinṭār is seven thousand dinars.
And Allah knows best what He intended.
The meaning of "المقنطرة" in the language is: completed, as you say: ألفٌ مؤلَّفةٌ (a thousand made complete).
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ إِن تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لاَّ يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ إِلاَّ مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَآئِماً﴾.
That is, persistent and not falling short, as you say: So-and-so is standing by (qāʾim bi-) his work.
Sībawayh said: دَامَ means ثَبَتَ (remained fixed).
Abū Jaʿfar said: And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ, he "forbade urinating in standing (al-dāʾim) water", i.e. still, stationary water.
﴿ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُواْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي ٱلأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾.
It was said: when the Jews traded with the Muslims they would say: There is no blame upon us in wronging them, because they oppose us. By "the unlettered" they meant the Arabs.
They were attributed to what the community (al-umma) was in before learning to write.
It was said: they were attributed to the mother (al-umm), and from this is "the unlettered Prophet". It was said: it is attributed to Umm al-Qurā, which is Mecca.

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿بَلَىٰ مَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقَى فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
بلى is a rejoinder to their saying ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الأمِّييِّنَ سَبِيلٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً أُوْلَـٰئِكَ لاَ خَلاَقَ لَهُمْ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
الخلاقُ is a share.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and al-Ashʿath ibn Qays related from the Prophet ﷺ that he ﷺ said: "Whoever swears a false oath in order to cut off by it the property of a Muslim man will meet Allah while He is angry with him." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً أُوْلَـٰئِكَ لاَ خَلاَقَ لَهُمْ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ وَلاَ يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ to the end of the verse.
There are two views on His saying ﴿وَلاَ يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾:
One of them: that it is related that Allah makes His friends hear His speech.
The other view: that He is angry with them, as you say: So-and-so does not speak to so-and-so.
The meaning of ﴿وَلاَ يُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ is: He will not praise them nor purify them; ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾, i.e. painful.
It is said: أألَمَ when it causes pain, so it is مؤلِمٌ; and "أَلِيمٌ" is for intensification.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْهُمْ لَفَرِيقاً يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: يلْوُونَ means they distort.
The philologists said: لويتُ الشيء when you turn it away from its course and take it otherwise than its [true] interpretation.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن كُونُواْ رَبَّانِيِّينَ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الربانيُّ is the learned jurist.
Abū Razīn said: he is the forbearing scholar.
The Arabs bring the alif and nūn for intensification, as in their saying:
جُمَّانيٌّ for one with a great mass of hair (jumma); and likewise سَكْران, i.e. full of intoxication.
So the meaning of al-rabbānī is: the one learned in the religion of the Lord (al-Rabb), who acts upon his knowledge — because if he does not act upon his knowledge he is not a scholar.
It is related from Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya that when Ibn ʿAbbās died he said: "The rabbānī of this community has died."
The meaning of ﴿وَلَـٰكِن كُونُواْ رَبَّانِيِّينَ﴾ is: but he says: Be rabbāniyyīn; then [the verb] was omitted because the hearer knows it.
Ibn Zayd said: the «ربانيون» are the rulers, and the aḥbār are the scholars.
Mujāhid said: the «ربانيون» are above the aḥbār.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is good, because the aḥbār are the scholars, and the rabbānī is one who combines with knowledge insight into governance; it is taken from the Arabs' saying: ربَّ أمرَ النَّاس يَرُبُّه when he set the people's affair right and undertook it; so he is رابٌّ, and ربَّانِيُّ is for intensification.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْمُرَكُمْ أَن تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ وَٱلنَّبِيِّيْنَ أَرْبَاباً﴾.
Whoever reads ﴿وَلاَ يَأْمُرَكُمْ﴾ in the accusative (naṣb), its meaning for him is: nor would the human being command you, because it is conjoined to what precedes it.
Whoever reads ﴿وَلاَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ﴾ in the nominative (rafʿ), its meaning for him is: nor does Allah command you. So said Sībawayh.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّيْنَ لَمَآ آتَيْتُكُم مِّن كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ﴾.
Ṭāwūs said: Allah took the covenant of the first of the prophets that he would believe in what the later one brought.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُ﴾.
He said: This verse is for the People of the Book; Allah took their covenant that they would believe in Muḥammad ﷺ and affirm him.
Ibn Masʿūd read: ﴿وَإذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الذَّيِنَ أُوتُوا الكِتَابَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He only took the covenant of the prophets binding upon their peoples.
Al-Kisāʾī said: "And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets" may mean: and when Allah took the covenant of those with the prophets.
The Basrans said: When Allah took the covenant of the prophets, He thereby took the covenant of those with them, because they followed them and affirmed them.
And "مَا" means "that which" (al-ladhī); it may also be conditional. It is also read "لِمَا" with kasra on the lām, in which case "مَا" also means "that which" and it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أخذ.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read: "لَمَّا" with doubling (tashdīd).
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلَىٰ ذٰلِكُمْ إِصْرِي﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. My covenant. And الإِصْرُ in the language is a heavy burden; the covenant was called iṣr because it is a restraint and a tightening.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَٱشْهَدُواْ وَأَنَاْ مَعَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلشَّاهِدِينَ﴾.
That is, make it clear, because the witness is the one who makes clear the reality of a thing.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ ٱللَّهِ تَبْغُونَ﴾.
That is, do you seek? So the meaning is: say to them, O Muḥammad: Is it other than the religion of Allah that you seek? Whoever reads ﴿يَبْغونَ﴾ with yāʾ, the speech in his view is consistent, because before it is ﴿فَمَنْ تَوَلَّى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمْ الفَاسِقُونَ﴾.
So the meaning is: Is it other than the religion of Allah that these seek?
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً﴾.
The meaning of ﴿وَلَهُ أسْلَم﴾ is: submitted; then He said ﴿طَوْعَاً وَكَرْهَا﴾.
It was said: since the practice regarding whoever opposed was that he be fought, his Islam was called unwilling, even if it was willing, because its cause was fighting.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿كَيْفَ يَهْدِي ٱللَّهُ قَوْماً كَفَرُواْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ﴾? [verse 86].
Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind related from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that a man of the Anṣār apostatised.
Mujāhid said: He was "al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd ibn al-Ṣāmit al-Anṣārī". He joined the idolaters, then regretted it, and sent to his people: Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whether there is any repentance for me. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿كَيْفَ يَهْدِي ٱللَّهُ قَوْماً كَفَرُواْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ﴾? up to His saying ﴿إلاَّ الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَأَصْلَحوا فَإنَّ الله غَفُورٌ رَحيم﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: So he became Muslim.
Al-Ḥasan said: It was revealed about the Jews, because they used to give the glad tidings of the Prophet ﷺ and seek victory over those who disbelieved [through him]; then when he was sent they were obstinate and disbelieved.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
If it is asked: Do the people of their own religion curse them? — there are several answers to this:
One of them: that some of them will curse others on the Day of Resurrection.
Another answer: that by "people" He means the Muslims.
It was said — and it is the best of them — that all people curse them, because they say: May Allah curse the wrongdoers, as He the Exalted said: ﴿أَلاَ لَعْنَةُ اللهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمين﴾.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿خَالِدينَ فِيهَا﴾, i.e. in the curse; the meaning is: in the punishment of the curse.

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِن تُطِيعُواْ فَرِيقاً مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ يَرُدُّوكُم بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ كَافِرِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: Allah warned you against them because they altered their scripture.
And in the ḥadīth: "Do not believe the People of the Book in what you do not know, nor call them liars, for they will not guide you when they have led themselves astray."

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ ثُمَّ ٱزْدَادُواْ كُفْراً لَّن تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهُمْ﴾.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: These are people who displayed repentance but did not make it real.
Others said: It was revealed about people who apostatised and joined the idolaters, then said: We will return and become Muslim.
So the meaning is that they too displayed repentance while concealing the opposite. The evidence for that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلضَّآلُّونَ﴾; had they made their repentance real, they would not have been called "those who are astray".
It is possible in the language that the meaning is: their repentance will not be accepted for the sins they repented of while they persist in disbelief; this is related from Abū al-ʿĀliya.
It is also possible that the meaning is: their repentance will not be accepted if they turn to another disbelief; their repentance is only accepted if they turn to Islam.

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ فَلَن يُقْبَلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِم مِّلْءُ ٱلأَرْضِ ذَهَباً وَلَوِ ٱفْتَدَىٰ بِهِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِّن نَّاصِرِينَ﴾.
Anas ibn Mālik related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"The disbeliever will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: Do you think, if you had the earth's fill of gold, would you ransom yourself with it?
He will say: Yes. It will be said to him: You have lied; you were asked for less than this. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ فَلَن يُقْبَلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِم مِّلْءُ ٱلأَرْضِ ذَهَباً﴾ to the end of the verse."
Some philologists said: the wāw is intrusive (muqḥama); the meaning is: the earth's fill of gold will not be accepted from any of them if he ransomed himself with it.
The analytical scholars among the grammarians said: It is not permissible for the wāw to be intrusive, because it indicates a meaning.
The meaning of the verse is: the earth's fill of gold will not be accepted [from] any of them as a voluntary gift, nor even if he offered it as ransom.
And المِلْءُ is the quantity that fills a thing, while المَلأُ with fatḥa is the maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿لَن تَنَالُواْ ٱلْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنْفِقُواْ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ﴾.
Ibn Masʿūd and ʿAmr ibn Maymūn said: البرُّ is Paradise; on this view the implied construction (taqdīr) is: you will not attain the reward of righteousness.
Others said: البِرُّ is righteous deeds. In the ḥadīth: "Hold to truthfulness, for it leads to righteousness (birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise; and beware of lying, for it leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire."
Anas ibn Mālik related that when this verse was revealed, Abū Ṭalḥa said: "I give my land in charity." The Prophet ﷺ commanded him to give it in charity to his relatives, so he divided it between Ubayy and Ḥassān.
It is related that ʿUmar wrote to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī to buy him a slave-girl — when the cities of Kisrā were conquered — so he bought her and sent her to him. When he saw her he was pleased with her; then he freed her and recited: ﴿لَن تَنَالُواْ ٱلْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنْفِقُواْ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is like His saying the Exalted ﴿وَيُطْعمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلى حُبِّهِ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا﴾ is: until you give in charity.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا تُنْفِقُواْ مِن شَيْءٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
That is, and since He knows it, He will requite it.

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلُّ ٱلطَّعَامِ كَانَ حِـلاًّ لِّبَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ إِلاَّ مَا حَرَّمَ إِسْرَائِيلُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تُنَزَّلَ ٱلتَّوْرَاةُ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He suffered from sciatica (ʿirq al-nasā) — so it is related from him — and he would cry out (lahu zaqāʾ, meaning crying out); so he swore that if he recovered from that he would not eat a vein (ʿirq).
Mujāhid said: What he forbade himself was cattle (al-anʿām).
ʿAṭāʾ said: He forbade the meat of camels and their milk.
All of this is correct as to what he forbade; and the Jews forbid it to this day, as their forebears did. There is a ḥadīth with a connected chain (musnad) on it.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: This was forbidden to us in the Torah. So Allah declared them liars and informed that Isrāʾīl forbade it to himself before the Torah was revealed, and He challenged them to produce it, saying: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُواْ بِٱلتَّوْرَاةِ فَٱتْلُوهَا إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكاً﴾.
Abū Dharr said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ: Which mosque was placed on earth first? He said: The Sacred Mosque. I said: Then which? He said: Then Bayt al-Maqdis. I said: How long was there between them? He said: Forty years. Then wherever the prayer finds you, pray, for it is a mosque."
Isrāʾīl related from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Khālid ibn ʿArʿara, who said: "A man asked ʿAlī about the first house placed for mankind — the one at Bakka — is it the first house on earth? He said: No, but it is the first house in which blessing, guidance and the Station of Ibrāhīm were placed, ﴿ومَنْ دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِنَاً﴾. Allah revealed to Ibrāhīm, Allah's blessings be upon him: Build Me a house — and he felt unequal to it — so Allah sent the Sakīna, which is a twisting (khajūj) wind with a head, and it marked out (naẓẓarat) the site of the House." [Translator's note: «فنَظَّرَتْ» is translated as written; the sense of "marked out / showed" is inferred.]
Abū al-Ḥasan said: Abū Bakr said: الخَجُوج is the wind that twists (takhujju) in its blowing, i.e. coils. It is said: خَجَّتْ تَخُجُّ; and if it were doubled it would be said: خَجْخَجَتْ; and khajkhaja is used to describe speed.
ʿAṭiyya said: "بكَّةُ" is the site of the House, and "مكةُ" is what is around it.
ʿIkrima said: "بكَّةُ" is what adjoins the House, and "مكَّةُ" is what is beyond that.
What most philologists hold is that "بكة" and "مكة" are one, and that the mīm may be a substitute for the bāʾ; one says لازِبٌ and لازمٌ (sticking), and سَبَدَ شعرهَ and سَمَدَه when he shaved it off from the root.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: It was called Bakka because people throng (yatabākkūn) in it, i.e. crowd one another in it.
Others said: It was called "Bakka" because it breaks (tabukku) the necks of tyrants; and on this view the mīm is a substitute for the bāʾ.
It may also be from their saying: امتَكَّ الفصِيلُ الناقةَ when the young camel sucks the she-camel hard [and drains her]. The first is better.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّـنَاتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid and the people of Mecca read: ﴿فِيهِ آيَةٌ بَيِّنَةٌ﴾.
Mujāhid explained that, saying: ﴿مَقَامُ إبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ is the whole Sanctuary; so he held that among its signs are "al-Ṣafā", "al-Marwa", "the Corner" and "the Station".
Whoever reads ﴿آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ﴾, his reading is clearer, because al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the signs; and among them is that a bird does not fly over the House while healthy.
Among them is that the hunting animal pursues the game, and when it enters the Sanctuary it leaves it. Among them is that when rain falls on the side of the Yemeni Corner, there is fertility in Yemen; when it is on the side of the Syrian [Corner], there is fertility in Syria; and when it covers the whole House, there is fertility in all lands.
Among them is that the [stoning] pebbles, however much is added to them, are seen to be of one size.
And المَقَامُ is from their saying: قُمْتُ مُقَامَاً (I stood a standing). As for the saying of Zuhayr:
وَفِيهِمْ مَقَامَاتٌ حِسَانٌ وُجُوهُهَا * وَأَنْدِيَةٌ يَنْتَابُها القَوْلُ وَالفِعْلُ
(Among them are assemblies whose faces are fair, and gatherings frequented by word and deed.)
its meaning is: among them are the people of assemblies.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً﴾.
Qatāda said: That too is among the signs of the Sanctuary.
This is a good view, because people used to be snatched away from all around it, yet no tyrant reached it; Bayt al-Maqdis was reached and destroyed, but the Sanctuary was not reached. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَلَمْ تَر كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحابِ الفِيل﴾.
Al-Thawrī related from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Whoever commits a ḥadd offence in the Sanctuary, it is carried out on him there; and if he commits it outside the Sanctuary and then enters the Sanctuary, he is not spoken to, not sat with and not traded with until he leaves the Sanctuary, and then the ḥadd is carried out on him.
Most of the Kufans said: That applies to every ḥadd that takes a life.
Some said: The security here is for game.
The most fitting of them is the first view, and it is general. Had it been for game, it would have been "وَمَا دَخَلَهُ" (whatever enters it) and not ﴿وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ﴾ (whoever enters it).
Qatāda said: It only means: whoever entered it in the Jāhiliyya was safe.
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ حِجُّ ٱلْبَيْتِ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Ibn al-Zubayr said: Whoever finds strength and the means to bear [the journey].
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Provisions and a mount.
Ḥammād ibn Salama related from Ḥumayd and Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, that a man said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the way to it? He said: Provisions and a mount.
السبيلُ in origin is reaching; from it the road is called sabīl. So the meaning according to the philologists is: whoever is able to reach the House; as He said, reporting [their words]: ﴿يَقُولُونَ هَلْ إلَى مَرَدٍّ مِنْ سَبِيل﴾?
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱلله غَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
Most commentators hold that the meaning is: whoever says that the ḥajj is not obligatory has disbelieved.
Wakīʿ related from Fiṭr, from Nufayʿ Abū Dāwūd, that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about this verse ﴿وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱلله غَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever performs the ḥajj not hoping for its reward, or stays at home not fearing its punishment, has disbelieved in it."
Al-Shaʿbī said: The way (al-sabīl) is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, makes easy.
This is among the good things said about it, i.e. according to capacity. Al-sabīl in the speech of the Arabs is the road; so whoever finds a road to the ḥajj without an impediment — chronic illness, incapacity, an enemy, or the unavailability of water on his route — the ḥajj is obligatory upon him; and whoever is prevented by any of these things has not found a road, because istiṭāʿa is the ability to do a thing. So whoever is incapable for some reason is not capable of it and is not able to find a way to it.
The most fitting of the views on the meaning of ﴿وَمَنْ كَفَر﴾ is: whoever denies Allah's obligation, because it comes right after the obligation of the ḥajj.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتُ ٱللَّهِ وَفِيكُمْ رَسُولُهُ﴾.
Al-Akhfash "Saʿīd ibn Masʿada" said: The meaning of "كيف" is: in what state?
Others said: The meaning of ﴿وَفِيكُمْ رَسُولُهُ﴾ is: he makes things clear to you.
It is possible that this address includes those who did not see the Prophet ﷺ, because his legacy and his Sunna are equivalent to witnessing him.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يَعْتَصِم بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾.
The meaning of "يَعْتَصِمْ" is: protects himself.

nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: "حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ" is: "that He be thanked and not denied, obeyed and not disobeyed, and remembered and not forgotten."
This is also related from the Prophet ﷺ.
Qatāda said: This verse was abrogated by His saying the Exalted ﴿فَاتَّقُوا الله مَا استْطَعْتُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is not possible for abrogating and abrogated to occur in this, because Allah the Exalted does not burden people except with what they are able.
His saying ﴿فَاتَّقُوا الله مَا استْطَعْتُمْ﴾ explains His saying ﴿ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ﴾; and it is what Ibn Masʿūd explained: that one remember Allah when it is obligatory upon him and not forget Him.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَمُوتُنَّ إِلاَّ وَأَنْتُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ﴾.
The meaning is: remain upon Islam until death comes to you while you are Muslims, because it is known that He does not forbid them what is not in their power.
Sībawayh reported: لا أَرَيَنَّك ها هنا (let me not see you here) — he did not forbid himself; the meaning is only: do not be here, for whoever is here, I will see him.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱعْتَصِمُواْ بِحَبْلِ ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعاً وَلاَ تَفَرَّقُواْ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The rope of Allah is the Qurʾān.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The rope is the covenant.
Al-Aʿshā said:
وَإذَا تُجوّزَهَا حِبَالُ قَبِيلَةٍ * أَخَذَتْ مِنَ الأُخْرَى إِليْكَ حِبَالُها
(And whenever the ropes [pledges of protection] of one tribe let her pass, she took from the next its ropes [to bring her] to you.)
The origin of al-ḥabl in the language is a means (sabab); from it the well-rope is named, because it is the means by which one reaches what is in it.
From it is said: "فلانٌ يَحطُبَ في حَبْلٍ فلانٍ" (so-and-so gathers firewood into so-and-so's rope), i.e. he inclines to him and his causes. The origin of this is that the wood-gatherer cuts the branches of trees and puts them in his rope; so when someone else cuts and puts them in his rope, it is said: he gathers wood in his rope.
From it is their saying: "حبلُكِ على غَارِبِكِ" (your rope is on your withers), i.e. I have released you from my bond (سَبْي) [Translator's note: «سَبْي» is probably a misprint for «سَبَبي», "my tie"], my command and my prohibition.
The origin of this is that when camels are let loose to graze, their ropes are thrown on their withers, so that they do not catch on thorns or other things and so keep them from grazing.
The meaning of ﴿وَلاَ تَفَرَّقُوا﴾ is: ولا تتفرَّقوا; then one of the two tāʾs was omitted. This was said to them because the Jews and the Christians split apart and declared one another disbelievers.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ كُنْتُمْ أَعْدَآءً فَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ بِنِعْمَتِهِ إِخْوَاناً﴾.
ʿIkrima said: This is about the Anṣār; there were evils between them, and Allah reconciled them through Islam.
It was said: it is general to Quraysh, because some of them used to raid others; then when they entered Islam their blood was made inviolable to one another, and they became brothers, i.e. each aims at what the other aims at.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفْرَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ فَأَنقَذَكُمْ مِّنْهَا﴾.
This is a figurative representation (tamthīl). And "الشَّفَا" is the edge; from it is أشقى فلانٌ على كذا [Translator's note: so in the text; the expression is «أشفى», with fāʾ] when he is on the brink of it.

nahhas-meani:104-104.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلْتَكُن مِّنْكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى ٱلْخَيْرِ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: الأمَّةُ is the group. And "مِنْ" here is not "partitive" (li-l-tabʿīḍ); it is only "for explaining the genus" (li-bayān al-jins), as He the Exalted said: ﴿فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأَوْثَانِ﴾.
He did not command them to avoid some of the idols; the meaning is only: avoid the filth which is the idols.

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ﴾.
Their whitening is their radiance, as He the Exalted said: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفرَةٌ﴾.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ أَكْفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ؟ فَذُوقُواْ ٱلْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾.
There is something omitted in the speech; the meaning is: As for those whose faces have blackened, it will be said to them: Did you disbelieve after your faith?
The grammarians agree that the fāʾ is necessary in the answer of "أَمَّا", because the meaning of your saying "أمَّا زيدٌ فمنطلقٌ" is: whatever may be the case, Zayd is departing.
Mujāhid said concerning His saying the Exalted ﴿أَكَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ﴾: after the taking of the covenant.
What indicates this is His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿وَإذْ أَخَذَ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ﴾, the verse.
It was said: They are the Jews, who gave glad tidings of the Prophet ﷺ and then disbelieved in him after he was sent; so it was said to them: Did you disbelieve after your faith?
It was said: It is general, i.e. did you disbelieve after you were small children, to whom the rulings of the believers applied?

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ٱبْيَضَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فَفِي رَحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿فَفِي رَحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾ is: in the reward of Allah's mercy.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ﴾.
It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "We complete seventy nations; we are the last of them and the most honoured of them before Allah."
Abū Hurayra said: "We are the best of people for people; we drive them in chains to Islam."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was revealed about those who emigrated with the Prophet ﷺ from Mecca to Medina.
It was said: the meaning of ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ is: you were [so] in the Preserved Tablet.
It was said: you have been [so] since you believed.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid: ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ — he said: on this condition: that you command what is right and forbid what is wrong; then He made it clear.
ʿAṭiyya said: You bore witness for the prophets — Allah's blessings be upon them all — whose peoples disbelieved in them, that they had conveyed [the message].
Then He made clear the goodness that is in them, saying: ﴿تَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنْكَرِ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ﴾.
Then He made clear that faith in Allah is not accepted except with faith in the Prophet ﷺ and what he brought, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ آمَنَ أَهْلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَكَانَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ مِّنْهُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ ٱلْفَاسِقُونَ﴾.
And الفاسقُ is the one who departs from the truth.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَن يَضُرُّوكُمْ إِلاَّ أَذًى وَإِن يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ ٱلأَدْبَارَ﴾.
He the Exalted made known that the Jews would not harm the Muslims except by distortion or slander; as for prevailing, it would not be theirs.

nahhas-meani:112-112.t:
He the Exalted made known that they are abased, saying: ﴿ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ أَيْنَ مَا ثُقِفُوۤاْ إِلاَّ بِحَبْلٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَحَبْلٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The rope is the covenant.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an exception not of the [same kind as the] first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); the meaning is: abasement has been struck upon them wherever they are found, except that they hold fast to a rope from Allah and a rope from people — meaning the protection (dhimma) they have.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَبَآءُوا بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, they returned; and it was said: they bore [it].
Its reality in the language is that it clung to them; and تبوَّأ فلانٌ الدَّار (so-and-so settled in the house) is from this, i.e. he kept to it.
Then He the Exalted informed why He did that to them, saying: ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلأَنْبِيَآءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ ذٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوْاْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعْتَدُونَ﴾.
And الاعتداءُ is overstepping [bounds].

nahhas-meani:113-113.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they are not equal, and that among them are some who have believed, saying, Glorified is He: ﴿لَيْسَوا سَوَاءً﴾.
That is, those of them who believed and those who disbelieved are not equal!?
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ أُمَّةٌ قَآئِمَةٌ يَتْلُونَ آيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ﴾.
﴿قائمة﴾: Mujāhid said: i.e. just.
﴿يَتْلُونَ آيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ﴾: al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: its hours.
The singular is إنْيٌ; one also says إِنْوٌ, and one also says إِنَىً.

nahhas-meani:114-114.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنْكَرِ﴾.
Commanding what is right here is commanding the following of the Prophet ﷺ.
﴿وَيَنْهَونَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ﴾, i.e. they forbid opposing him ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:115-115.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَمَا يَفْعَلُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ يُكْفَروهُ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
Whoever reads "وَمَا يَفْعَلوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ يُكْفَرُوهُ", in his view it refers to these people mentioned, and whoever does good is in their position.
Whoever reads "وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ تُكْفَرُوهُ" with tāʾ, it is general.

nahhas-meani:117-117.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ مَا يُنْفِقُونَ فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ فِيهَا صِرٌّ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: الصِرُّ is cold.
The meaning of صِرّ in the language: al-ṣirr is intense cold. And in the ḥadīth: (that he forbade the locusts killed by al-ṣirr).
The meaning of the verse: He likened what they spend on fighting the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, in its futility, to a wind that ﴿أَصَابَتْ حَرْثَ قَوْمٍ ظَلَمُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَأَهْلَكَتْهُ﴾, i.e. the crops of a people whom Allah punished with that, so their crops perished; likewise the deeds of these people — they will get nothing back from them.

nahhas-meani:118-118.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ بِطَانَةً مِّن دُونِكُمْ لاَ يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالاً﴾.
البطانةُ are a man's intimates, to whom he discloses the inner part of his affairs.
The meaning is: do not take intimates from other than the people of your religion.
A parallel to this is ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾.
Likewise ﴿فَسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾, i.e. upon the people of your religion and those who stand in your place.
The meaning of His saying the Exalted ﴿لاَ يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالاً﴾ is: they do not fall short in [doing you] evil.
The origin of الخَبَال in the language is from الخَبْل, and الخَبْل is the loss of a thing and its corruption.
And His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَدُّواْ مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾.
That is, what is hard and severe for you.
The origin of this is that it is said: عَنِت العظمُ يَعْنَتُ عَنَتَاً when the bone breaks after having been set.
From this is His saying the Exalted ﴿ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ العَنَتَ مِنْكُمْ﴾, i.e. hardship.

nahhas-meani:119-119.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَآأَنْتُمْ أُوْلاۤءِ تُحِبُّونَهُمْ وَلاَ يُحِبُّونَكُمْ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْكِتَابِ كُلِّهِ﴾.
That is, you love the hypocrites and they do not love you.
The evidence that He means the hypocrites is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا لَقُوكُمْ قَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْاْ عَضُّواْ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلأَنَامِلَ مِنَ ٱلْغَيْظِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: They bite the tips of their fingers out of rage.

nahhas-meani:120-120.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ وَإِن تُصِبْكُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَفْرَحُواْ بِهَا﴾.
That is, if you take booty or are victorious, that grieves them; and if the opposite of that befalls you, they rejoice at it.
Then He informed that if they are patient in that, it will not harm them at all, saying: ﴿وَإِن تَصْبِرُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئاً إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:121-121.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ تُبَوِّىءُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَقَاعِدَ لِلْقِتَالِ﴾.
﴿تُبَوِّىءُ﴾ means: you make [them] keep to; and بَاءَ بكذا when one is bound to it.
It is related that the Prophet ﷺ saw [in a dream] that he was in a strong coat of mail, and he interpreted that as Medina; so he commanded his Companions to stay in it until the idolaters arrived, and then fight them.

nahhas-meani:122-122.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ هَمَّتْ طَّآئِفَتَانِ مِنكُمْ أَن تَفْشَلاَ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُمَا﴾.
Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: We are they — "Banū Salima" and "Banū Ḥāritha" of the Aws — and it would not please us had it not [been revealed], because of His saying the Exalted ﴿وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُمَا﴾.
And الفَشَلُ in the language is cowardice; and al-walī is the helper.
"Banū Salima" are of the Khazraj, and "Banū Ḥāritha" are of the Aws. [Translator's note: the text earlier says both clans are "of the Aws"; this last line corrects it.]

nahhas-meani:123-123.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ وَأَنْتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ﴾.
It was said: by "humble" (adhilla) He means that they were few in number.
Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said: "We used to say among ourselves that the number of the people of Badr was like the number of the companions of Ṭālūt, and they were three hundred and some ten [-odd]."
Whoever reads "بِثَلاَثَةْ آلافٍ مِنَ المَلاَئِكَةِ مُنْزلِينَ". [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off here in the source.]

nahhas-meani:125-125.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلَىۤ إِن تَصْبِرُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ وَيَأْتُوكُمْ مِّن فَوْرِهِمْ هَـٰذَا﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿIkrima said: from this direction of theirs.
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِخَمْسَةِ آلاۤفٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ﴾.
We know of no disagreement that the meaning of "مُسَوِّمِينَ" is from al-sūma (a distinguishing mark), except from al-Akhfash, for he said: "مُسَوِّمِينَ" means sent forth.
Abū Zayd said: al-sūma is that the horseman marks himself in battle to display his courage.
ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: The angels on the day of Badr were on piebald horses, wearing yellow turbans.
Abū Isḥāq said: Their mark was white turbans.
Al-Ḥasan said: They put marks of white wool on the tails and forelocks of their horses.
ʿIkrima said: Upon them was the mark of battle.
Mujāhid said: The wool on the horses' tails.
It was also read ﴿مُسَوِّمِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: so vocalised in the text, identical to the lemma; the variant meant is presumably the other vocalisation, مُسَوَّمِين / مُسَوِّمِين], and the proponent of this reading adduced as evidence that it is related that the Prophet ﷺ said to them on the day of Badr: "Mark yourselves, for I have seen that the angels have marked themselves."
That is, they had marked their horses, or themselves.

nahhas-meani:126-126.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ بُشْرَىٰ لَكُمْ﴾.
He means the reinforcement, or the promise.

nahhas-meani:127-127.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفاً مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ فَيَنقَلِبُواْ خَآئِبِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: "يَكْبِتَهُمْ" means: grieve them.
It is related that the Prophet ﷺ "came to Abū Ṭalḥa and saw his son downcast (makbūt), and said: What is the matter with him? It was said: His little bird (nughayr) has died."
So al-makbūt here is the grieved one.
Abū ʿUbayda said: It is said: كَبَتَهُ لوجهِهِ, i.e. he threw him down on his face.
It is well known in the language that one says: كَبَتَه when he humiliated him and abased him.
Some philologists said: كَبَتَه means كَبَدَه (struck his liver); then tāʾ was substituted for the dāl, because their points of articulation are in one place.
And الخائبُ in the language is the one who has not obtained what he hoped for; it is the opposite of al-mufliḥ (the successful).
